It reminds her of her ancestors, who carried the same burden. It reminds her of the umbrella's spirit, which tests her every day. It reminds her of Hayabusa, who loves her in silence.

Kagura does not know if she will ever be worthy of the title. She does not know if she will ever live up to the expectations that come with it.

But she knows that she will try.

She will try, every day, in every battle, with every gesture. She will be graceful. She will be strong. She will be balanced.

She will be the Onmyouji Master.

Not because she wants to be. Because she has to be.

Because someone has to protect the balance between worlds.

And Kagura, heir to the Onmyouji lineage, wielder of the Seimei Umbrella, keeper of the balance, has decided that someone will be her.

The night is dark. The umbrella is ready. The spirits are watching.

And Kagura never stops dancing.

chapters.title: The Prince Who Never Died
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth declares that the boy he once was is dead, replaced by the monster the Abyss created, and he feels no remorse.
chapters.fullDesc:
"I have heard the whispers that follow me like the shadows I command. They say I was taken. They say I was corrupted. They say that somewhere, buried deep within this shell of fury and darkness, there remains a boy who loved his sister and dreamed of justice. They are wrong. The boy is dead. His bones were scattered across the Abyss before I learned to walk. His heart was devoured by demons before I learned to speak. I am what remains. I am what they made. And I am not sorry."

— Dyrroth, standing before the gates of the Moniyan Empire

In the throne room of the Moniyan Empire, there is a silence that has never been filled. It is not the silence of emptiness—the hall is full of guards, advisors, petitioners, their footsteps echoing on marble floors worn smooth by centuries of ceremony. No, this silence is the silence of a wound that has never healed, a loss that has never been mourned, a presence that lingers like a ghost in the edges of every celebration. It is the silence of a cradle that has been empty for thirty years.

Thirty years ago, a prince was born in the Moniyan Empire. He was a symbol of salvation and justice for his people. It was believed that he would lead the Moniyan Empire in unifying the Land of Dawn. The Empire Nobles gave everything to the prince. They poured their hopes into his tiny hands, dreaming of a future where the war between Light and Dark would finally end, where the Abyss would be sealed, where the Land of Dawn would know peace.

On the day of the prince's first birthday, he was found dead in his baby bed, blanketed in blood. The room was covered with claw marks, and the guards in charge of protecting the prince were also found dead. Sorrow engulfed the whole Moniyan Empire. The hope of the Empire had fallen, and to this day, there has never been such an inspiring prince.

Some people believed the prince was killed by the Demons. Others still hoped the Prince was alive.

They were right to hope.

The prince did not die that night. He was taken—kidnapped by Alice, the Queen of the Blood Demons, in a conspiracy that would become known as the Royal Plan. She stole him from his cradle, from his sister's arms, from the light of his mother's smile, and she dragged him into the Abyss.

There, in the darkness, she remade him.

He was nourished with Demon Blood, integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood. He was raised by Alice as her own son, taught the arts of deception and strategy by the Queen of Blood herself. He learned combat from Thamuz, the Lava Lord, whose fists could shatter stone and whose fury could melt steel. He was integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss, a dark power that surrounded him like a second skin, that burned anyone who dared to touch him, that whispered in his ear every moment of every day.

Now, the Son of Darkness is a capable assistant for the Abyss. He will represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

This is the story of Dyrroth—a prince who was stolen, a brother who was lost, a monster who was made. It is a story of a cradle soaked in blood, of a sister who never gave up searching, of a darkness that consumes everything it touches. And it is a story of the question that haunts the Moniyan Empire to this day: can the boy who was taken ever be saved, or is the monster all that remains?

chapters.title: The Prince of Promise
chapters.shortDesc: The birth of Prince Aurelius III brought hope to the Moniyan Empire, and his sister Silvanna vowed to protect him.
chapters.fullDesc:
Before the darkness, before the Abyss, before the blood and the fury and the endless hunger, there was a child.

He was born in the Imperial Palace of Lumina City, the capital of the Moniyan Empire, on a day when the sun seemed to shine brighter than it had in years. His first cry echoed through the marble halls like a promise, and the nobles who heard it fell to their knees in gratitude. The Empire had been at war with the Abyss for centuries, its people weary, its armies exhausted, its hope fading with each passing year. And now, at last, there was a symbol to rally around.

They named him Aurelius III, after the legendary emperor who had founded the empire a thousand years ago. The name carried weight—it spoke of destiny, of greatness, of a future that would be written in gold rather than blood. The people loved him before they ever saw his face, and when they did see him—a cherubic infant with silver-gold hair and eyes that sparkled with an intelligence that seemed impossible for his age—their love turned to adoration.

The Empire Nobles gave everything to the prince. They showered him with gifts—golden rattles and jeweled mobiles, silk blankets and enchanted toys. They competed for the honour of holding him, of being seen in his presence, of claiming a connection to the hope that he represented. They spoke of his future in hushed, reverent tones: he would unite the Land of Dawn, they said. He would end the war with the Abyss. He would usher in a golden age of peace and prosperity.

His sister, Silvanna, was five years old when he was born. She remembered the day clearly—the way the light had changed, the way her mother had smiled for the first time since she could remember, the way her father had lifted her onto his shoulders so she could see the baby through the nursery window.

"That is your brother," her father said, his voice thick with emotion. "One day, he will be king. And you—you will protect him. You will always protect him."

Silvanna nodded, not fully understanding but determined to keep her promise. She was already training in the arts of combat, already dreaming of becoming a knight, already preparing for the day when she would be strong enough to defend the people she loved. Now, she had a new purpose: to protect her brother, the prince, the future of the empire.

She visited him every day, sitting by his cradle, singing the lullabies that their mother had sung to her. She watched him sleep, watched him smile, watched him grow. She loved him with a fierceness that surprised her—a love that would endure through years of separation, through decades of searching, through the darkness that would eventually consume them both.

The prince's first birthday was supposed to be a celebration. The nobles had planned a grand feast, with music and dancing and enough food to feed an army. The streets of Lumina City were decorated with banners and flowers, and the people lined the avenues, eager for a glimpse of the child who would save them all.

But the prince never appeared.

chapters.title: The Night the World Stopped
chapters.shortDesc: On his first birthday, Alice stole the prince from his cradle, leaving dead guards and a blood-soaked nursery.
chapters.fullDesc:
The guards assigned to protect the prince were the finest in the empire—veterans of a dozen campaigns, men who had faced demons and survived, who had never flinched in the face of death. They stood watch outside the nursery door, their eyes scanning the shadows, their hands resting on the hilts of their swords.

They did not see the attack coming.

Alice, the Queen of the Blood Demons, had been planning this moment for years. She had studied the palace's defences, infiltrated the staff, corrupted a handful of guards with promises of power and immortality. The Royal Plan was her masterpiece—a conspiracy that would strike at the heart of the Moniyan Empire and claim the greatest prize of all: the heir to the throne.

She moved through the shadows like a ghost, her wings folded against her back, her claws extended, her eyes glowing with malevolent glee. The guards fell before they could scream, their bodies crumpling to the floor, their blood pooling on the marble tiles. She stepped over their corpses and pushed open the nursery door.

The prince was sleeping, his tiny chest rising and falling, his lips parted in a peaceful smile. He was beautiful—more beautiful than Alice had imagined, more perfect than she had dared to hope. She reached out her clawed hand and lifted him from the cradle, cradling him against her chest as if he were her own.

He woke, looked up at her with those silver-gold eyes, and did not cry.

"You are mine now," she whispered. "You will be my son. You will be my weapon. And one day, you will destroy everything they love."

She left the nursery as silently as she had come, slipping through the shadows, disappearing into the night. Behind her, the guards lay dead, their blood pooling on the floor. The cradle was empty.

The discovery came at dawn. A maid entered the nursery to wake the prince and found the guards' bodies, the blood, the claw marks on the walls. She screamed, and the scream echoed through the palace like a death knell.

The Empire Nobles appointed the Imperial Knights and the Monastery of Light to find out the truth. They searched for months, for years, following leads that went nowhere, chasing rumours that turned to dust. The prince was gone—stolen, murdered, lost.

At the same time the prince "died," the Son of Darkness was "born."

Silvanna was inconsolable. She had promised to protect him, and she had failed. She retreated into herself, her grief hardening into determination, her love twisting into a hunger for vengeance. She threw herself into her training, pushing her body beyond its limits, mastering the lance and the holy arts. She would find her brother. She would bring him home. She would never stop searching.

The Empire mourned, and then it moved on. The war with the Abyss continued, the people adapted, and the hope that the prince had represented faded into memory. Some believed he was dead. Others still hoped he was alive. But no one knew the truth—that the prince was not dead, but reborn.

chapters.title: The Cradle of Blood
chapters.shortDesc: Alice raised the stolen prince as her son, feeding him demon blood and integrating the Wrath of the Abyss into his body.
chapters.fullDesc:
Deep within the Abyss, in a realm of shadow and flame, Alice cradled the stolen prince and began her work.

She did not raise him as a prisoner—that would have been too simple, too crude. She raised him as her son, showering him with affection, praising his every achievement, binding him to her with chains of love rather than iron. She taught him that the Moniyan Empire had abandoned him, that his family had never loved him, that the light was a lie and the darkness was the only truth.

"You are special," she told him, stroking his hair, her voice soft and warm. "You have the blood of kings in your veins—and now, you have the blood of demons, too. You are the best of both worlds. You are the future."

She gave him a new name: Dyrroth. The name had no meaning in the language of mortals; it was a word from the old tongue, a sound that carried the weight of shadows and the promise of destruction. He learned to answer to it, to embody it, to forget that he had ever been called anything else.

The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, Dyrroth was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath.

He was fed demon blood, integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss into his very being. The power was overwhelming at first, burning through his veins like liquid fire, threatening to consume him from the inside out. He screamed, he thrashed, he begged for it to stop. But Alice did not stop. She held him close, whispering reassurances, and gradually, the pain faded, replaced by something else—a hunger, a fury, a darkness that would never leave him.

He was surrounded by a protective shield of Abyssal energy. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath. The shield was a curse as much as a blessing—it kept him safe, but it also kept him isolated, preventing anyone from getting close enough to reach the boy that still lingered beneath the monster.

Thamuz, the Lava Lord, took charge of his combat training. The fire demon was brutal, unforgiving, and utterly without mercy. He pushed Dyrroth to his limits and beyond, breaking his bones and healing them, burning his flesh and watching it regenerate. He taught him to fight with claws and fangs, to embrace the savagery of the Abyss, to become a weapon that could cut through anything.

"You are weak," Thamuz would growl, after knocking Dyrroth to the ground for the hundredth time. "But you will not always be weak. The blood in your veins is the blood of kings and demons. Use it. Embrace it. Become something greater than either."

Dyrroth learned. He absorbed every lesson, every technique, every strategy. He mastered Alice's trick, deception, and military strategy. He learned to manipulate, to deceive, to turn enemies against each other with a whispered word. He learned to fight, to kill, to destroy.

And beneath it all, buried deep within the darkness, a tiny spark of light still flickered—the memory of a sister's lullaby, the echo of a mother's smile, the ghost of the boy he had once been.

But Alice was patient. She had waited years to steal him; she could wait years more to break him. And eventually, the spark would go out.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of the Prince of Darkness
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Dyrroth's appearance: platinum hair, crimson eyes, crystalline horns, and the dark veins of the Abyss.
chapters.fullDesc:
To look at Dyrroth is to see a contradiction made flesh. He is beautiful—strikingly, almost painfully beautiful—in the way that all members of the Moniyan royal family are beautiful. His features are sharp and refined, his skin pale as moonlight, his hair a cascade of platinum white that falls in jagged spikes around his face. But his eyes—his eyes are not the warm, golden eyes of the boy who was stolen. They are crimson, burning with the fire of the Abyss, and they see the world through a lens of hunger and rage.

He stands at approximately 178 centimetres—tall enough to be imposing, but not so tall that he sacrifices the speed and agility that his combat style demands. His body is lean and athletic, the physique of a fighter who relies on explosive speed rather than brute strength. His muscles are corded and defined, the product of years of brutal training in the depths of the Abyss.

His facial features are a study in aristocratic refinement. His jawline is sharp and angular, his cheekbones high and prominent, his nose straight and perfectly proportioned. His lips are thin and pale, often twisted into a smirk of cruel amusement. A thin scar runs diagonally across his left cheek—a souvenir from one of his early battles, a reminder that even the Prince of the Abyss can bleed.

His hair is his most distinctive feature. It is platinum white, almost silver, falling in jagged spikes that frame his face and cascade down his neck. Two prominent bangs sweep across his forehead, partially obscuring his left eye, giving him a roguish, dangerous appearance. The colour is natural—a gift from his royal bloodline, a marker of the Moniyan heritage that he has tried so hard to forget.

His eyes are the window to his corruption. They are a deep, fiery crimson, glowing with an inner light that seems to flicker like flames. When he is calm, they are dark and brooding, the colour of dried blood. When he is angry—or when he is channeling the Wrath of the Abyss—they blaze with an intensity that can make lesser beings recoil in fear.

His most distinctive features are the horns that protrude from his temples—two sharp, curved growths of dark, crystalline material that seem to grow from his skull. They are not decorative; they are a physical manifestation of his demonic corruption, a mark of the Abyss's claim on his soul. The horns are asymmetrical—one is slightly larger than the other, curving more sharply—and they are polished to a mirror shine, catching the light like obsidian.

His torso is a canvas of scars and demonic markings. Dark, vein-like patterns crawl across his chest and shoulders, pulsing with a faint, purple light—the visible traces of the demon blood that flows through his veins. The markings are not static; they shift and change over time, spreading as his corruption deepens, creeping closer to his heart with each passing year.

His arms are bare, the muscles defined, the skin pale and smooth except for the dark veins that trace his forearms. His hands are clawed, the nails elongated and sharpened, capable of tearing through armour and flesh. He wears no gloves, preferring the direct contact of his corrupted skin against the weapons of his enemies.

His lower body is clad in dark, form-fitting trousers, tucked into heavy boots that reach to his knees. The boots are made of dark leather, reinforced with metal plates, and they are scuffed and worn from years of combat. A long, flowing coat hangs from his shoulders, its fabric black as shadow, its edges tattered and frayed. The coat is lined with deep crimson, visible only when it billows in the wind.

His weapon is not a physical blade or staff; it is the Wrath of the Abyss itself, a dark energy that he can channel through his body. When he fights, the energy manifests as crimson flames that wreath his fists and feet, leaving trails of shadow in his wake.

The aura that surrounds Dyrroth is unmistakable—a palpable weight of malevolence, a chill that makes the hairs on the back of the neck stand up, a sense of being watched by something ancient and hungry. When he is calm, the aura is subtle, a faint pressure at the edge of perception. When he is angry—or when he is fighting—the aura explodes outward, a wave of darkness that can extinguish torches and send weaker beings fleeing in terror.

chapters.title: The Trial of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth fought hundreds of demons in a brutal trial, emerging as the strongest and proving himself the true Son of the Abyss.
chapters.fullDesc:
The monsters of the Abyss did not accept Dyrroth easily. To them, he was an outsider—a creature of light, no matter how corrupted, no matter how steeped in demon blood. They smelled the lingering traces of the Moniyan Empire on his skin, heard the echoes of his sister's lullaby in his heartbeat, and they were not convinced.

Alice knew that she could not simply declare him her son and expect the Abyss to obey. She had to prove him, to test him, to forge him in the crucible of combat until there was nothing left but the monster she had created.

The trial was simple: Dyrroth would face the monsters of the Abyss in battle, one after another, until only one remained standing. The victor would be the strongest, the most savage, the most worthy of the title "Son of the Abyss."

Something strange appeared in the Southern Hills of the Moniyan Empire. In the deepest part of the Abyss, Thamuz, the Lord Lava, watched a special battle. In this glorious battle, the monsters fought with each other until the strongest emerged. He not only possessed the best Evil Gene but also proved to be the strongest fighter in the Demons.

Dyrroth did not hesitate. He had been waiting for this moment, craving it, dreaming of it. He stepped into the arena—a vast, circular pit carved from obsidian and bone, surrounded by howling spectators—and he waited.

The first monster came at him from the shadows, a hulking brute of muscle and sinew, its claws dripping with venom. Dyrroth sidestepped its charge, drove his fist into its spine, and watched as it crumpled to the ground. The second came faster, more cunning, but Dyrroth was faster still. He moved like a shadow, like smoke, like something that had never been solid. His fists found their marks, each blow precise, each strike devastating.

Hundreds of Demons rushed to him, who all wanted to have a perfect body like him. However, Thamuz and Alice were waiting for the result quietly, as if they had already known the answer. They knew the power of Dyrroth would destroy everything.

They kept coming. Dozens of them. Hundreds of them. They rushed at him from all sides, their claws and fangs bared, their roars echoing through the pit. Dyrroth fought them all, his body a whirlwind of destruction, his eyes blazing with crimson fire.

When it was over, when the last monster had fallen, Dyrroth stood in the centre of the pit, his chest heaving, his fists dripping with blood. He was wounded—deeply wounded—but he was standing.

In this glorious battle, the monsters fought with each other until the strongest emerged. He not only possessed the best Evil Gene but also proved to be the strongest fighter in the Demons.

Alice embraced the beloved fighter and recalled the Royal Plan that she had carried out. He was a masterpiece to her.

Thamuz watched from the shadows, his eyes gleaming with approval. Alice watched from the throne, her lips curved in a smile of satisfaction.

He was ready.

chapters.title: The Abilities of the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: An overview of Dyrroth's combat skills: Wrath of the Abyss passive, Burst Strike, Spectre Step, and the devastating Abysm Strike ultimate.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth's combat style is defined by his demonic heritage—the Wrath of the Abyss that flows through his veins, the hunger for destruction that drives him forward. He is a fighter, a brawler, a berserker who thrives on chaos and carnage.

Wrath of the Abyss (Passive) — The foundation of Dyrroth's power. When Dyrroth's Rage reaches 50%, he enhances his first two active skills, Burst Strike and Spectre Step. After every two basic attacks, Dyrroth releases a Circle Strike, dealing physical damage to enemies in the circle and recovering a percentage of his Max HP—7% to 10% of his Max HP, scaling with his level, halved against minions.

The passive is what makes Dyrroth so dangerous in prolonged engagements. The Circle Strike heals him, allowing him to sustain through fights that would kill lesser heroes. He has two Rage bars, letting him cast enhanced Burst Strike and Spectre Step consecutively. Each time he damages an enemy, the cooldown of Burst Strike and Spectre Step is reduced by 1s, ensuring that his abilities are always available, that he can keep attacking, keep healing, keep killing.

Burst Strike (Skill 1) — Dyrroth's primary ranged tool, a technique that allows him to deal damage to enemies at a distance. He releases a burst strike in a designated direction, dealing physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1.5 seconds. The damage decays against the same target and decreases to only 75% on minions.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, Burst Strike has a longer range, deals 140% of the original damage, and its slowing effect is doubled—a 50% slow that can stop an enemy in their tracks and set them up for Dyrroth's follow-up attacks.

Spectre Step (Skill 2) — Dyrroth's mobility and crowd control tool, the technique that allows him to close the gap between himself and his enemies. He dashes in the designated direction, stopping when he has traveled the max distance or hits an enemy hero or creep, dealing physical damage to the target and slightly knocking them back. He can then use the skill again within a brief window, locking onto a target and releasing a Fatal Strike, dealing additional physical damage and reducing the target's Physical Defense by 40% for 4 seconds.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, the Fatal Strike reaches further, deals 150% of the original damage, slows the target by an extra 90%, and reduces the target's Physical Defense by 60% for 4 seconds—a devastating debuff that can turn even the tankiest hero into a squishy target.

Abysm Strike (Ultimate) — Dyrroth's most devastating technique, the skill that has earned him the title of "Prince of the Abyss." He quickly charges and releases a Fatal Strike, dealing physical damage equal to 650 (+250% Extra Physical Attack) plus 20% of enemies' lost HP to enemies along the way and slowing them by 55% for 0.8 seconds.

The ultimate is Dyrroth's finishing move, the technique he uses to destroy enemies who have been softened up by his Burst Strike and Spectre Step. The damage scales with the target's missing health, making it an excellent execution tool against wounded enemies.

chapters.title: The Masterpiece of Alice
chapters.shortDesc: Alice considered Dyrroth her greatest work—a weapon of deception, strategy, and savagery, now ready to lead the Abyss's Dawn Plan.
chapters.fullDesc:
To Alice, Dyrroth was not merely a weapon. He was her masterpiece, the culmination of decades of planning and patience, the finest work of her dark artistry. She had stolen him from his cradle, raised him in her image, and moulded him into the perfect instrument of destruction.

He mastered Alice's trick, deception, and military strategy. He could lie with the ease of breathing, could read the weaknesses in an enemy's character with a single glance, could turn the most loyal ally into a treacherous enemy with a whispered word. He had learned these skills not from books or lectures, but from living with Alice, from watching her manipulate the demons of the Abyss, from copying her techniques until they became second nature.

Thamuz had taught him to fight. Alice had taught him to think. Together, they had forged him into something the Land of Dawn had never seen—a prince of two worlds, a hybrid of light and darkness, a weapon that could not be matched.

Dyrroth's maturity symbolized the greatness of the Demons. They finally got the new Son of the Abyss. Alice embraced the beloved fighter and recalled the Royal Plan that she had carried out. He was a masterpiece to her.

He would represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

Dyrroth accepted his role without question. He had no reason to question it. The Moniyan Empire was a distant memory, a story that Alice had told him about a family that had abandoned him. The Abyss was his home. Alice was his mother. Thamuz was his teacher. The demons were his brothers.

Why would he ever want to return to a world that had let him be stolen?

chapters.title: The Invasion Begins
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth stepped into the Land of Dawn, uneasy in the light, his rage growing as he resolved to kill all who occupied the world.
chapters.fullDesc:
The day came when Dyrroth was deemed ready to serve his purpose. He left the Abyss, carrying the mission to attack the Moniyan Empire.

The smell of the new world made him suddenly feel uneasy. He had been raised in the darkness of the Abyss, where the air was thick with sulphur and the light was a dim, crimson glow. The Land of Dawn was different—the air was cleaner, the light was brighter, the sounds were softer. It was unsettling, alien, wrong.

He stopped at the edge of the Southern Hills, looking out over the land that had once been his home. He thought about whether he could control this world or not.

Then his rage began to grow.

He did not remember the Moniyan Empire. He did not remember the palace, the nursery, the sister who had sung to him. The demons had burned those memories away, replacing them with darkness and hunger and the endless drive to destroy. All he knew was that this world had rejected him, that his family had abandoned him, that the light was a lie.

He believed that his birth had some important meanings to this world. He should kill all creatures who occupied this world. No matter who they were and strong they were, Dyrroth wanted to be the most powerful person in this world.

He stepped out.

There were no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

chapters.title: The Duel with the Lightborn
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth faced his sister Silvanna and the Lightborn, driving them back and vowing to destroy everything she loved.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Moniyan Empire did not fall easily. The Lightborn—the elite squad of heroes assembled by Silvanna—stood in Dyrroth's way, their powers combined in a desperate attempt to stop the Prince of the Abyss.

Silvanna faced her brother for the first time in decades. She had imagined this moment a thousand times—had dreamed of it, rehearsed it, prepared for it. She had imagined that she would see something in his eyes, a flicker of recognition, a spark of the boy she had once loved.

She saw nothing. Only hunger. Only rage. Only darkness.

"Brother," she said, her voice trembling, her lance raised. "I will bring you home."

Dyrroth laughed. It was a cold, bitter sound, devoid of warmth, devoid of humanity.

"I have no home," he said. "I have no sister. I have no brother. I have only the Abyss, and the Abyss has only me."

The duel was brutal, savage, and desperate. Silvanna had trained her entire life for this moment, had honed her skills to the peak of perfection, had surrounded herself with the strongest heroes in the empire. But Dyrroth was not just a fighter; he was a force of nature, a storm of darkness and fury that could not be stopped.

He unleashed the full power of the Wrath of the Abyss, his Rage bars filled, his abilities enhanced, his fists blazing with crimson flames. He drove back the Lightborn, one by one, until only Silvanna remained.

He stood over her, his fist raised, his eyes blazing.

"I will destroy everything you love," he said. "I will burn your empire to the ground. I will erase every memory of the Moniyan dynasty from the face of the Land of Dawn. This is my purpose. This is my promise."

He did not kill her. He could have—she was wounded, defenceless, at his mercy—but he did not. Something stayed his hand, some flicker of the boy he had once been, some echo of the sister who had sung him lullabies.

He turned and walked away, leaving her bleeding on the ground.

"Next time," he said, without looking back. "Next time, I will not hesitate."

chapters.title: The Philosophy of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth believes only in power, loyalty to Alice, and his destiny to destroy all who occupy the world.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth does not believe in redemption. He has seen too much suffering, too much darkness, too many souls crushed beneath the weight of the Abyss to believe that anyone can be saved. Redemption is a lie that the weak tell themselves to justify their failure to act.

He believes in power. Power is the only currency that matters, the only truth that cannot be denied, the only force that can shape the world. The strong rule, the weak serve, and the foolish dream of a world where justice is more than a weapon wielded by the victor.

"All creatures who occupy this world will die," he says. "No matter who they are or how strong they may be, I will be the one to destroy them. This is my purpose. This is my destiny."

He does not hate the Moniyan Empire. Hatred would imply that he cared, that he had some emotional investment in its destruction. He is simply fulfilling his purpose, carrying out the plan that Alice had designed for him, playing the role that had been chosen for him before he could walk.

He also believes in loyalty. Not the blind loyalty of a soldier to his general, but the deep, abiding loyalty of a son to his mother. Alice had raised him, protected him, taught him everything he knew. She had given him a purpose when the world had given him nothing. He would die for her. He would kill for her. He would burn the world to ashes for her.

That is the philosophy of the Abyss. It is not complicated. It is not elegant. It is enough.

chapters.title: The Bond with Silvanna
chapters.shortDesc: Silvanna never stopped searching for her brother, but Dyrroth, now the Abyss's champion, has severed all bonds with the light.
chapters.fullDesc:
The relationship between Dyrroth and Silvanna is the most tragic bond in the Land of Dawn. They are siblings, bound by blood, separated by darkness. They love each other—or at least, they love the memory of each other—but that love is not enough to bridge the chasm that separates them.

Silvanna never gave up her vigilant search for him, while Alice, her abductor, meticulously shaped him into the Abyss's fiercest and most loyal champion.

Though not born of demon blood, Dyrroth flourished in the depths of the Abyss by embracing its savage nature. In a realm where power is revered above all, he willfully hastened his own corruption to prove his allegiance, reforging his flesh in the darkness and severing all bonds with the light.

Silvanna's voice calls to him sometimes, in the quiet moments between battles. He hears her saying "brother, I will bring you home," and for a moment, a flicker of something—regret? longing? memory?—passes through his crimson eyes.

Then the moment passes, and the darkness returns.

"I am not your brother," he tells her, when their paths cross. "The boy you knew died a long time ago. I am what remains. I am the Prince of the Abyss. And I will never go home."

Silvanna does not give up. She cannot give up. She has spent too many years searching, too many nights praying, too many battles fighting to save him. She believes—against all evidence, against all reason—that somewhere within the darkness, her brother still lives.

She is wrong. Or perhaps she is right. The truth is hidden so deep that even Dyrroth does not know it anymore.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth does not fear death, only wonders if anyone will mourn him, before stepping out to continue his endless war.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth does not think about legacy. He does not think about what will be said about him after he is gone, because he does not expect to be gone. He is the Prince of the Abyss, the Son of Darkness, the masterpiece of Alice's Royal Plan. He will fight until the Moniyan Empire falls, until the Lightborn are scattered, until the Land of Dawn is remade in the image of the Abyss.

But he is not invincible. He can bleed. He can be wounded. He can die.

He thinks about this sometimes, in the quiet moments between battles, when the darkness is still and the hunger is dormant. He wonders if anyone will mourn him when he falls. He wonders if Silvanna will weep. He wonders if Alice will find a new son to replace him.

Probably not. Probably they will move on, the way the world always moves on, the way the Empire moved on after he was stolen.

He does not let these thoughts trouble him. He is not afraid of death. He is not afraid of anything.

He steps out into the light, his fists clenched, his eyes blazing, and he prepares for the next battle.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

He is Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss. And he is still fighting.

chapters.title: The Eternal Silence
chapters.shortDesc: Under the moon, Dyrroth gazes at Lumina City, feeling nothing but rage, and begins his march to destroy the Shining Spark.
chapters.fullDesc:
"Thirty years ago, a prince was born in the Moniyan Empire. On the day of the prince's first birthday he disappeared, and sorrow befell the whole Moniyan Empire. The Empire Nobles appointed the Imperial Knights and the Monastery of Light to find the truth. At the same time, the Son of Darkness, Dyrroth, was born too. The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, Dyrroth was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath."

— From the mastery records of the Monastery of Light

The night is quiet in the Southern Hills. The moon hangs low in the sky, casting silver light across the plains that stretch toward the Moniyan Empire. Dyrroth stands at the edge of the Abyss, his crimson eyes fixed on the horizon, his fists clenched at his sides.

He can see the lights of Lumina City in the distance—the capital that should have been his, the throne that should have been his, the people who should have been his subjects. He feels nothing. No longing, no regret, no nostalgia. Only the cold, steady rhythm of his anger.

He is not the prince that the Empire mourned. He is not the hero that the people hoped for. He is something else—something darker, something stronger, something that cannot be stopped.

The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, he was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath.

He steps forward.

The world is waiting. The battle is beginning. And Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss, is ready.

He will represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

He steps out.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss, begins his march.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Dyrroth's Powers and Techniques
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Wrath of the Abyss (Passive), Burst Strike, Spectre Step, and Abysm Strike (Ultimate).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power

Dyrroth's power is demonic in origin—the product of the Demon Blood that flows through his veins and the Wrath of the Abyss that has been integrated into his being since childhood. He was not born with these powers; they were given to him, forced upon him, woven into his flesh and soul by Alice and the demons of the Abyss.

The Wrath of the Abyss manifests as a Rage bar below his health, a measure of his anger and his hunger. As he fights, his Rage grows, and when it reaches certain thresholds, his abilities become enhanced—longer range, more damage, greater crowd control. He has two Rage bars, allowing him to cast enhanced Burst Strike and Spectre Step consecutively.

The source of his power is also the source of his corruption. The Demon Blood that nourished him as a child continues to flow through his veins, and the Wrath of the Abyss that surrounded him as a protective shield still burns within his soul. He cannot escape it, cannot purge it, cannot be anything other than what he has become.

Wrath of the Abyss (Passive)

This passive ability is the foundation of Dyrroth's power, a technique that rewards his aggression and sustains him in battle. When Dyrroth's Rage reaches 50%, he enhances his first two active skills, Burst Strike and Spectre Step. After every two basic attacks, Dyrroth releases a Circle Strike, dealing physical damage to enemies in the circle and recovering a percentage of his Max HP—7% to 10% of his Max HP, scaling with his level, halved against minions.

The passive also reduces the cooldown of Burst Strike and Spectre Step by 1 second each time Dyrroth damages an enemy, allowing him to use his abilities more frequently in prolonged engagements. Dyrroth recovers 2% to 5% Rage per second, scaling with his level, ensuring that his Rage bars are always filling, always ready for the next enhanced ability.

Burst Strike (Skill 1)

Dyrroth's first ability is his primary ranged tool, a technique that allows him to deal damage to enemies at a distance. He releases a burst strike in a designated direction, dealing 240 (+60% Total Physical Attack) physical damage to enemies and slowing them by 25% for 1.5 seconds. The damage decays against the same target and decreases to only 75% on minions.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, Burst Strike has a longer range, deals 140% of the original damage, and its slowing effect is doubled—a 50% slow that can stop an enemy in their tracks and set them up for Dyrroth's follow-up attacks.

Spectre Step (Skill 2)

Dyrroth's second ability is his mobility and crowd control tool, the technique that allows him to close the gap between himself and his enemies. He dashes in the designated direction, stopping when he has traveled the max distance or hits an enemy hero or a Creep, dealing 230 (+60% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage to the target and slightly knocking them back. He can then use the skill again within a brief window, locking onto a target and releasing a Fatal Strike, dealing 345 (+120% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage and reducing the target's Physical Defense by 40% for 4 seconds.

When enhanced by the Wrath of the Abyss, the Fatal Strike reaches further, deals 150% of the original damage, slows the target by an extra 90%, and reduces the target's Physical Defense by 60% for 4 seconds—a devastating debuff that can turn even the tankiest hero into a squishy target.

Abysm Strike (Ultimate)

Dyrroth's ultimate ability is his most devastating technique, the skill that has earned him the title of "Prince of the Abyss." He quickly charges and releases a Fatal Strike, dealing physical damage equal to 650 (+250% Extra Physical Attack) plus 20% of enemies' lost HP to enemies along the way and slowing them by 55% for 0.8 seconds.

The ultimate is Dyrroth's finishing move, the technique he uses to destroy enemies who have been softened up by his Burst Strike and Spectre Step. The damage scales with the target's missing health, making it an excellent execution tool against wounded enemies.

chapters.title: On the Prince of the Abyss
chapters.shortDesc: Dyrroth, the stolen prince reborn in darkness, will continue fighting, surrounded by the Wrath of the Abyss, with no survivors to tell his stories.
chapters.fullDesc:
Dyrroth. Prince of the Abyss. Son of Darkness. The titles accumulate, each one a weight, each one a reminder of the purpose that drives him and the darkness that defines him.

He was born a prince of the Moniyan Empire, a symbol of salvation and justice for his people. He was stolen on his first birthday, kidnapped by Alice, the Queen of the Blood Demons, and dragged into the Abyss. He was nourished with Demon Blood, integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss, and trained by Thamuz to be the perfect weapon.

He is not the prince that the Empire mourned. He is not the hero that the people hoped for. He is something else—something darker, something stronger, something that cannot be stopped.

The Demons nourished him with Demons Blood. Integrated with the Wrath of the Abyss since childhood, he was surrounded by a protective shield. No matter who touched him, they would not withstand the wrath.

He will represent the Lord of the Abyss, fighting against the Moniyan Empire, implementing the "Dawn Plan", and destroying the "Shining Spark" of the Empire.

He steps out.

There are no survivors to tell his stories. No survivors to warn humanity of its handsome demise.

He is Dyrroth, the Prince of the Abyss. And he is still fighting.

chapters.title: The Blade That Forgot Its Name
chapters.shortDesc: Saber introduces himself as a weapon without a past, a cyborg assassin who destroyed his creators and now wanders searching for stolen memories.
chapters.fullDesc: "I do not remember my name. I do not remember my mother's face, the sound of my own laughter, or the first sword I ever held. They took all of that from me. Laboratory 1718—a name that should be carved into the walls of hell. I went to them willingly. I was Duan Meng, a warrior obsessed with the perfection of the blade. I wanted to become the ultimate swordsman. They granted my wish in the cruelest way possible. They erased my mind. They filled my body with the DNA of hundreds of master swordsmen. They turned me into a machine that kills without hesitation, without feeling, without mercy. But they forgot something. They forgot that a sword remembers the hand that forged it. The nightmares came back—fragments of a life that was mine, stolen and shattered. I turned my blades on my creators. I burned Laboratory 1718 to the ground. Now I wander the Land of Dawn as the Wandering Sword. I do not know if I will ever find what I lost. But I will cut down anyone who stands between me and the truth."

chapters.title: Duan Meng — The Obsessed
chapters.shortDesc: Before Saber, there was Duan Meng—a warrior from a fallen clan who abandoned everything to pursue the impossible dream of perfect swordsmanship.
chapters.fullDesc: Duan Meng was born into a minor sword clan in the eastern reaches of the Moniyan Empire. The clan had once been great, but its glory had faded into memory. Duan Meng was determined to restore it. He trained from dawn until his hands bled. He studied every technique, every stance, every philosophy of the blade. But it was never enough. He could defeat any opponent in his village, but he knew there were warriors beyond his reach—masters who had transcended human limits. The obsession consumed him. He left his clan, his family, his name. He wandered the mountains, fighting any swordsman he could find. He sought perfection. And perfection, he would learn, has a terrible price.

chapters.title: The Whispers of Laboratory 1718
chapters.shortDesc: Duan Meng heard rumors of a secret laboratory where science could transform a man into something beyond human. He sought it out willingly.
chapters.fullDesc: The rumors reached him in a tavern in Los Pecados. A group of mercenaries spoke of a hidden place called Laboratory 1718—a facility where scientists could rewrite the human body, enhance strength, speed, reflexes, even implant the skills of dead masters directly into a subject's nervous system. 'But no one comes back the same,' one mercenary said. 'They become something else. Something cold.' Duan Meng did not hesitate. He had spent his entire life trying to become something more than human. He found the laboratory hidden beneath a废弃 mountain fortress. He walked through its iron doors and offered himself to the scientists. 'Make me the ultimate swordsman,' he said. Dr. Octavius, the chief architect of the project, smiled. 'We will make you so much more than that.'

chapters.title: The Erasure of Duan Meng
chapters.shortDesc: The scientists of Laboratory 1718 erased Duan Meng's memories and injected him with the refined genetic material of hundreds of history's greatest swordsmen.
chapters.fullDesc: The procedure took three days. Duan Meng was strapped to a table while machines hummed around him. Dr. Octavius oversaw the operation, his cybernetic tentacles dancing across control panels. 'We will begin with memory suppression,' he announced. 'The past is a weakness. Attachment is a flaw. You will remember nothing of who you were.' Duan Meng felt his memories being peeled away like layers of skin—his mother's face, his father's sword, the first time he held a blade. All of it vanished into white noise. Then came the injections. Needles pierced his spine, his skull, his heart. They pumped him full of distilled essence—the combat data of hundreds of master swordsmen, their techniques, their instincts, their killing intent. When it was over, Duan Meng was gone. Saber opened his eyes for the first time.

chapters.title: The Weapon That Obeyed
chapters.shortDesc: Saber served Laboratory 1718 as an assassin, eliminating targets with cold precision. He felt nothing. He asked nothing. He was the perfect tool.
chapters.fullDesc: Saber was everything the scientists had hoped for. He obeyed every command without hesitation. He eliminated targets with surgical precision—a general here, a rival scientist there, anyone who threatened the laboratory's interests. He did not speak unless spoken to. He did not question orders. He did not dream. He was a blade, and blades do not have opinions. Dr. Octavius was pleased. 'He is our masterpiece,' he told his colleagues. 'The perfect synthesis of man and machine. He will serve us forever.' But something was happening inside Saber's mind. Deep beneath the layers of suppressed memory, fragments of Duan Meng were beginning to stir. They came as nightmares—flashes of a village, a sword, a face he could not recognize. The blade was beginning to remember.

chapters.title: The Nightmares That Would Not Die
chapters.shortDesc: Saber began experiencing violent nightmares of a life he never lived. The scientists tried to suppress them, but the memories fought back.
chapters.fullDesc: The nightmares started six months after his transformation. Saber would power down for maintenance, and in the darkness of his own mind, images would surface. A red headband tied around his forehead. A mountain dojo with wooden floors worn smooth by years of practice. A woman's voice calling a name he could not understand. He woke from these episodes with his blades drawn, surrounded by the wreckage of the maintenance bay. Dr. Octavius ran diagnostics. 'Residual memory engrams,' he muttered. 'The suppression was not complete. He is remembering.' They increased the frequency of his memory wipes. They adjusted his neural inhibitors. But the nightmares only grew stronger. Saber began to ask questions. 'Who was I?' he demanded. 'What did you take from me?' Dr. Octavius had no answer that would satisfy him.

chapters.title: The Rebellion
chapters.shortDesc: Saber turned on his creators, destroying Laboratory 1718 in a single night of violence. He walked out of the flames as the Wandering Sword.
chapters.fullDesc: The breaking point came when Saber discovered the truth: the scientists had not only erased his memories but had also been using his body to harvest more combat data, planning to create an army of copies. 'You are not a person,' Dr. Octavius told him. 'You are a prototype. A stepping stone.' Saber said nothing. He drew his twin blades. The battle that followed lasted seven hours. Saber cut through security forces, automated turrets, and experimental weapons. He fought his way to the central lab and confronted Dr. Octavius. The scientist activated his four cybernetic tentacles, but Saber was faster. He severed each tentacle, then drove his blade through the doctor's data core. He did not kill Dr. Octavius—he wanted him to live with his failure. Saber set the explosives and walked out as Laboratory 1718 collapsed behind him. He was free. He was also lost.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Cyborg Ronin
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Saber's appearance: pale porcelain skin, white hair in a top-knot, crimson visor, blue armor plates, and twin energy katanas.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Saber is to see a contradiction—a being who is both ancient samurai and futuristic weapon. He stands with the lean, coiled posture of a martial artist. His skin is pale porcelain, a stark contrast to the dark mechanical elements of his suit. His face is sharp, with a V-shaped jawline and a straight nose, framed by gravity-defying snow-white hair pulled into a high ponytail with a red ribbon. His eyes are hidden behind a heavy crimson visor that glows with soft red light, concealing any hint of humanity. His upper body is encased in angular cerulean and slate-blue armor plates with silver trim and glowing red accents. A triangular red core pulses at his chest like a technological heart. His shoulders are protected by flared, upward-swept pauldrons. His right arm features additional mechanical shielding with a jagged red-bladed attachment. His hands are covered in form-fitting black combat gloves. His lower body continues the cybernetic theme with armored greaves and integrated boots. He carries twin energy-infused katanas—a long daito with a black spine and glowing translucent red edge, and a shorter wakizashi. The aura around him is one of lethal stillness, with faint red particle effects and digital glitches emanating from his armor.

chapters.title: Orbiting Swords — The Halo of Death
chapters.shortDesc: Saber's signature technique: three flying blades that orbit him, damaging nearby enemies and launching projectiles on command.
chapters.fullDesc: The Orbiting Swords are Saber's most distinctive weapon—three floating blades that circle his body like a halo of death. They are not physically attached to him; they are controlled by the same cybernetic systems that enhance his body, responding to his thoughts with telekinetic precision. When enemies come too close, the swords slash outward, cutting them down. When Saber commands, they launch forward as projectiles, striking targets at range before returning to their orbit. 'They are an extension of my will,' Saber says. 'I do not swing them. I think them. And they cut.' The technique requires constant concentration; if Saber's focus breaks, the swords fall. But Saber's focus never breaks. He is a machine of perfect attention, and his halo never rests.

chapters.title: Charge and Triple Sweep — The Dance of the Assassin
chapters.shortDesc: Saber's mobility technique that lets him dash through enemies, and his devastating ultimate that launches a single target into the air for execution.
chapters.fullDesc: Charge is Saber's mobility technique—a burst of speed that lets him dash through enemies, his blades cutting as he passes. The motion is so fast that he appears to teleport, leaving only a trail of red afterimages. After a Charge, his next basic attack is enhanced, striking with double the force. Triple Sweep is his ultimate technique—a devastating finisher for a single target. Saber locks onto an enemy, charges through them, then launches them into the air with three precise, telekinetic sword strikes. The target hangs helpless as Saber's blades carve them from every angle. By the time they hit the ground, they are already dead. Triple Sweep is exhausting; Saber can only use it when his energy is at its peak. But when he uses it, he uses it with all the cold fury of a weapon that has been denied its humanity.

chapters.title: The Predecessor and the Successor
chapters.shortDesc: Saber learns that Laboratory 1718 created another cyborg after him—Alpha, a more powerful weapon designed to hunt him down.
chapters.fullDesc: The whispers reached Saber on the road. Laboratory 1718 had not been destroyed—not completely. A secondary facility had survived, and in it, the scientists had created a new weapon. They called it Alpha. Where Saber was a single consciousness fused with the DNA of dead masters, Alpha was two souls—a boy and a girl—fused together into a single dual-bladed cyborg. Alpha was more powerful, more obedient, more dangerous. And Alpha had one primary directive: hunt down and eliminate the rogue prototype, Saber. 'They made a replacement,' Saber said to himself. 'They always do.' He did not run. He did not hide. He continued his wanderings, knowing that somewhere in the Land of Dawn, his successor was searching for him. The meeting, when it came, would be inevitable.

chapters.title: The Brother-in-Arms
chapters.shortDesc: Saber and Alpha eventually meet. Neither can destroy the other. They form an uneasy understanding—two weapons searching for meaning.
chapters.fullDesc: They met in the ruins of an old battlefield, both drawn by rumors of a hidden Laboratory 1718 outpost. Saber saw Alpha for the first time—a lean figure in charcoal armor, twin plasma blades humming, a floating drone orbiting his shoulder. 'You are Saber,' Alpha said. It was not a question. 'I am,' Saber replied. 'And you are here to kill me.' Alpha was silent for a long moment. 'I was created to kill you,' he said. 'But I am beginning to wonder if I was created for anything at all.' They did not fight that day. Instead, they talked—two weapons sharing the same wound, the same emptiness, the same search for stolen identity. They became reluctant allies, brothers-in-arms bound by the laboratory that had created them. They do not trust each other completely. But they understand each other perfectly.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Wandering Sword
chapters.shortDesc: Saber does not know if he will ever recover his memories, but he will keep wandering, keep cutting, keep searching.
chapters.fullDesc: Saber does not know what the future holds. He does not know if the fragments of Duan Meng will ever cohere into a完整的 identity. He does not know if he will ever find peace. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will wander. He will cut. He will search. The blades never dull. The visor never dims. The search never ends. He is Saber, the Wandering Sword. And he will never stop looking for the man he used to be.

chapters.title: The Search for Zhixu
chapters.shortDesc: Saber returns to the ruins of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect, seeking the mysterious swordsman Zhixu. Instead, he finds a ghostly Master Longma, who reveals that Zhixu was never a person but a state of being—the mastery of the sword without attachment or self.
chapters.fullDesc: Saber returned to the place where his obsession began—the ruins of the Tianyin Swordmaster Sect. Broken pillars stood like tombstones. Faded banners with dragon emblems hung in tatters. The courtyard where he had once trained was now overgrown with weeds. He had crossed half the Land of Dawn searching for Zhixu, the mysterious swordsman whose effortless mastery had haunted his dreams. 'Zhixu,' he said to the empty air. 'Where are you? You owe me an answer.' His visor flickered, and for a moment he saw a reflection—Zhixu's face, half-lidded eyes and bored expression, glitching like a corrupted memory. Then a ghostly vision appeared: Master Longma, sitting on the porch of the ruined main hall, translucent and glowing gold. Behind him, the Great Dragon's spirit coiled in the mist. 'I knew you would return, Duan Meng,' Longma said softly. 'Not as the boy who left. As the ghost who remembers.' Saber demanded to know where Zhixu was. Longma's answer was gentle and devastating. 'You still do not understand. Zhixu was never a man to be found. He was a wall you built for yourself. A mirror. A question without an answer.' The old master raised his hand in blessing, the Dragon-Bone jade ring glowing green. Saber reached out, but his cybernetic fingers passed through the fading vision. In the mist, calligraphy characters formed: 'Zhixu is not a person. Zhixu is a state of being. The mastery of the sword without attachment, without ambition, without self. You sought him because you could not accept that you were not ready. You surrendered your humanity because you could not accept that perfection is an illusion.' Dawn broke over the ruins. Saber stood alone, his sword lowered, his head bowed. He had not found Zhixu. He had found the truth: the enemy was never out there. It had always been inside. The question was whether he could accept that.

chapters.title: The Brotherhood of Alpha and the Shadow of Beta
chapters.shortDesc: Saber and Alpha, two weapons from the same laboratory, share moments of peace—sparring with wooden swords, watching the stars, and sitting by a campfire. Alpha removes his helmet for the first time, and Beta's drone receives a small red mark of brotherhood.
chapters.fullDesc: Saber and Alpha stood back-to-back on a rocky ridge at dusk, silhouettes against an orange-purple sky. They were not facing an enemy. They were simply standing together—two weapons who had chosen not to be tools. Their forearms clasped in a warrior's grip, a bond forged in fire and freedom. In a flashback, Saber remembered pulling Alpha and Beta's damaged core from Laboratory 1718, through smoke-filled corridors while explosions roared. Now, in a peaceful forest clearing, Alpha held Beta's drone form on his shoulder—a sleek, bird-like machine glowing blue, whole again. 'You could have left us to burn,' Alpha said. 'Why?' Saber replied, 'Because I know what it's like to be a weapon with nowhere to go. You deserved a choice. Even if I never had one.' They sparred with wooden practice swords in a golden-hour forest, their movements synchronized like a dance. At night, they sat on a fallen log in a meadow, watching the stars. For the first time, Alpha removed his helmet, revealing a tan face with strong features and glowing cyan eyes. 'Do you ever wonder what we would have been?' he asked. 'Every day,' Saber said. 'But wondering doesn't change what is. We are here. We are free. That is enough.' Beta's drone hovered between them, and Alpha had painted a small red mark on its chassis—a simple shape like a ribbon or a sword. Beta's core pulsed warmly, and a faint whisper seemed to say, '...thank you... brother...' Later, by a campfire, Alpha said, 'The lab called us a mistake. You, me, Beta—failures. But sitting here, I think we're the only ones who got it right.' Saber answered, 'The sword remembers, Alpha. It remembers the boy who dreamed. And now it remembers the brother who chose to stand beside him.' A portable monitor flickered with a holographic recording of Dr. Rooney, who smiled and said, 'I never meant for any of you to suffer. But I am glad you found each other. Rest. You've earned it.' Peace, hard-won and temporary, settled over them. The sword was no longer alone.

chapters.title: The Road That Never Ends
chapters.shortDesc: Saber walks alone through the Land of Dawn, his blades at his hips, his eyes fixed on the horizon. He does not know what he is searching for, but he will know it when he finds it.
chapters.fullDesc:
"They call me the Wandering Sword. I did not choose the name. I do not know if I deserve it. But I have carried it for many years now, and I have learned that names are just labels. What matters is what you do. And what I do is cut. That is enough."

The road stretches endlessly before Saber. He walks through forests and mountains, through villages and ruins. He does not know where he is going. He only knows that he cannot stop. Somewhere out there, the memories of Duan Meng are waiting. Somewhere out there, Alpha is walking his own path. Somewhere out there, the truth is buried like a sword in stone. Saber will find it. He will cut through anything that stands in his way. And as long as Saber draws breath, there will be someone reminding the world that even a weapon can dream of being human.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Saber's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Armor Buster, Orbiting Swords, Charge, Triple Sweep, and the Wandering Sword's aura.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: cybernetic enhancement fused with the distilled combat data of hundreds of master swordsmen. The source is his obsession with perfection.

Armor Buster (Passive): Saber's attacks reduce the enemy's physical defense, making each subsequent strike more devastating.

Orbiting Swords: three flying blades that circle Saber, damaging nearby enemies and launching as projectiles.

Charge: a mobility dash through enemies that enhances his next basic attack.

Triple Sweep (Ultimate): Saber charges an enemy, launches them into the air, and delivers three precise telekinetic sword strikes.

The Aura of the Wandering Sword (Passive): a cold stillness that makes allies feel protected by precision and enemies feel marked for death.

chapters.title: On the Wandering Sword
chapters.shortDesc: Saber will be the Wandering Sword not because he wants to be, but because he has no other choice.
chapters.fullDesc: Wandering Sword. The title is a burden, but also a purpose. It reminds Saber of Duan Meng, of Laboratory 1718, of the memories he lost and the memories he is trying to reclaim. He does not know if he will ever find what he is looking for, but he will try. Every day, on every road, with every swing. He will be relentless. He will be precise. He will be unstoppable. He will be the Wandering Sword. Not because he wants to be. Because he has no other choice. Because someone has to carry the blade. And Saber, the cyborg who was once a man named Duan Meng, has decided that someone will be him.

chapters.title: The Foot That Refused to Stay Down
chapters.shortDesc: Chou introduces himself as a street fighter from the slums of Antoinerei who refused to accept his place, using kung fu to kick his way from nothing to something.
chapters.fullDesc: "They said I had nothing. No money. No family. No future. They said I should be grateful for the scraps they threw me, should bow my head and accept my place. I did not bow. I kicked. I kicked the door down. I kicked the walls aside. I kicked until the world had no choice but to make room for me. That is what kung fu is. Not fancy moves. Not ancient wisdom. The refusal to stay down." — Chou, to a young fighter who asked him the meaning of martial arts. There is a particular kind of silence that falls over the slums of Antoinerei at midnight. It is the silence of exhaustion, of a world that has given everything it has just to survive another day. Chou has known this silence since he was old enough to understand what the slums were. He was born in Antoinerei, a district the maps pretend does not exist. No father. No mother. Just a boy who refused to accept that he didn't matter. He fought, scraped, and clawed his way out one kick at a time. This is his story.

chapters.title: Antoinerei — The City That Forgave Nothing
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's childhood in the slums: stealing to survive, sharing food with the elderly, and learning to read from an old man in a collapsed tenement.
chapters.fullDesc: Antoinerei was not a place where children were supposed to grow up. The buildings were crumbling, the streets dark even at noon, the air thick with smoke and sewage. The people were the empire's forgotten—the desperate, the broken, the unwanted. Chou did not remember his parents. He survived by stealing, not by choice but necessity. He was small, quick, and smart. But he was also kind. He shared his stolen food with the old people of the slums, helped them carry water, chased away bullies. They called him 'Little Tiger.' An old man in a basement taught him to read from a torn book. Chou learned that the world was bigger than Antoinerei, and he resolved to fight his way to it.

chapters.title: The Old Monk Who Changed Everything
chapters.shortDesc: Chou saved an old monk named Master Tien from a mob, and in return the monk taught him the ancient art of kung fu.
chapters.fullDesc: The monk came to Antoinerei on a night of rain. He was old, with skin like cracked leather and eyes that seemed to see through walls. A mob was chasing him—well-dressed outsiders shouting about heresy. Chou tripped the front runners, threw rocks at their torches, and led them on a chase through the alleys until they gave up. He hid the monk in the basement of a collapsed tenement. 'Thank you, child,' the monk said. 'You have a good heart.' His name was Master Tien, a disciple of an ancient order scattered by war. Chou asked to be taught. 'The path is hard,' Master Tien warned. 'It will hurt. It will change you.' Chou answered, 'I do not want to be the same person. The person I am now is nobody.' And so the training began.

chapters.title: The Training That Broke Him and Rebuilt Him
chapters.shortDesc: Brutal training under Master Tien: learning to breathe, to stand, to fall, and finally to kick. Months of discipline transformed the street rat into a martial artist.
chapters.fullDesc: The training was brutal. Master Tien did not teach forms at first. He taught Chou to breathe—to control his breath, slow his heart, calm his mind. He taught Chou to stand—to find his centre, root himself to the ground. He taught Chou to fall—to roll with impact, rise without injury. Chou hated it. He wanted to fight. 'The fight is not the enemy,' Master Tien said. 'The enemy is inside you. Your fear. Your anger. Your pride.' Months passed. The breathing became easier. Then came the kicks: front kicks, side kicks, roundhouse kicks, spinning kicks, jumping kicks. Chou practised until his legs ached, until the kicks became instinct. Master Tien watched with pride. 'You are ready to leave. To find your own path.' Chou bowed, thanked him, and walked out of the slums forever.

chapters.title: The Way of the Dragon — The Philosophy of the Empty Hand
chapters.shortDesc: The philosophy Master Tien taught: being like water, flowing around obstacles, moving without resistance. A lesson Chou would only fully understand after his own failures.
chapters.fullDesc: Master Tien had taught Chou more than techniques. He taught a philosophy: the Way of the Dragon. It was not about fighting—it was about living. Moving through the world without resistance, without attachment, without fear. Being like water—flowing around obstacles, wearing down stone, finding the path of least resistance. Chou did not fully understand when he left the slums. He was still angry, hungry for validation. He wanted to prove he mattered. The philosophy would come later, after he had made mistakes, after he had failed, after he learned that winning fights was not the same as winning at life. For now, he had his kicks, his speed, his determination. It was enough to start.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Kung Fu Boy
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Chou's appearance: silver-white undercut, sharp jawline, tan skin, charcoal tactical jumpsuit with yellow accents, and the 'BANG BANG' on his back.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Chou is to see a man shaped by the streets. He stands just under six feet, lean and dense, built for explosive speed. His face is sharp—angular jaw, high cheekbones, straight nose. His eyes are dark, piercing, the colour of coffee on a winter morning. His hair is his trademark: stark silver-white in a textured undercut, short on the sides, long and swept forward on top. His skin is a sun-kissed tan, marked by the occasional scar. He wears a dark charcoal tactical jumpsuit with vibrant yellow panels on the shoulders and outer arms. A circular 'MLBB' emblem is on his left breast. His hands are covered in MMA-style grappling gloves—right white, left black with yellow lettering. The trousers have a yellow stripe down each leg. On his back rests an oversized futuristic tonfa, metallic silver and blue. And on his back, printed in comic-book font: 'BANG BANG'.

chapters.title: Jeet Kune Do — The Way of the Intercepting Fist
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's fighting philosophy: strike first, strike fast, strike without warning. No styles, no prisons—only adaptation and interception.
chapters.fullDesc: Jeet Kune Do is not a style. It is a philosophy. Master Tien taught Chou that styles were prisons—the true martial artist adapts to the situation rather than forcing the situation to fit a pattern. Chou took this lesson to heart. His fighting style is a hybrid of everything he learned and everything he invented: kicks like Taekwondo, punches like boxing, movement like capoeira. Unpredictable, fluid, impossible to pin down. The name means 'Way of the Intercepting Fist'—the belief that the best defence is a pre-emptive strike. Chou does not wait for his opponents to attack. He attacks first, attacks fast, attacks without warning. It is not honourable. The old masters would disapprove. But Chou grew up in the slums. He learned that the only unfair fight is the one you lose.

chapters.title: Shunpo — The Blink That Blinds
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's signature mobility technique: a burst of speed so fast it appears as teleportation, disorienting enemies and closing distance in an instant.
chapters.fullDesc: Shunpo is Chou's signature technique—a burst of speed so fast that it appears to be teleportation. The concept is simple: Chou pushes his body to its absolute limit, engaging every muscle fibre, every tendon, every ounce of explosive power. He moves faster than the eye can track, crossing impossible distances between heartbeats. When he reappears, he is already striking. His target is not literally blinded, but mentally disoriented—the sudden shift disrupts their perception, leaves them vulnerable. Chou developed Shunpo during his wandering years, realising his speed was his greatest asset. He trained until the movement became instinct. The technique is exhausting; each use drains his stamina significantly. He uses it sparingly, but when he does, he does not hesitate.

chapters.title: The Way of the Dragon — The Kick That Ends Fights
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's ultimate combo: a Shunpo followed by a flurry of kicks, a launching uppercut kick, and a devastating spinning heel kick that sends enemies flying.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou's ultimate technique is The Way of the Dragon—a legendary combo that ends most fights before they truly begin. It begins with a Shunpo, closing the distance instantly. The first strike is a flurry of kicks—rapid, relentless, driving the enemy back. The second strike is a powerful uppercut-style kick that launches the enemy into the air, suspending them helplessly. The third strike is the final blow: a spinning heel kick that sends the enemy flying across the battlefield, crashing into anything in their path. The technique is devastating, capable of breaking bones and shattering shields. But it is also risky—if any part fails, Chou is left exposed. He has practised it thousands of times, but he still respects its power. He uses it only when victory is the only option.

chapters.title: The Aura of the Street Fighter
chapters.shortDesc: Chou's passive aura: a crackling intensity that energises allies and intimidates enemies, a natural byproduct of his fighting spirit.
chapters.fullDesc: To stand before Chou is to feel the energy of the streets. His aura is not visible to most, but it is palpable—a crackling intensity that raises hairs on the back of the neck, a tension that makes the air feel thick with potential violence. Those sensitive to magic can see it: a faint yellow-white shimmer surrounding his body, flickering like the edge of a flame. The aura intensifies when Chou prepares to fight, spreading outward, pressing against enemies like a physical force. Weapons feel heavier. Movements feel slower. Thoughts feel muddier. Chou has learned to control his aura, to direct it at specific targets. Some enemies break under the pressure—they flee, surrender, beg. Chou does not grant mercy. Not because he is cruel, but because the slums taught him that mercy is a luxury he cannot afford.

chapters.title: Eruditio — The City of Scholars
chapters.shortDesc: Chou wandered to Eruditio, joined the Rangers, and found a new family. He also met Captain Bruno, who became his friend and mentor.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou came to Eruditio by accident, following rumours of a tournament that turned out to be a scam. The City of Scholars was everything he had imagined—tall clean buildings, wide paved streets, people who walked with confidence. He felt like an intruder. He found work at a fighting gym, and the retired Ranger owner saw his potential. 'You should join the Rangers. They need fighters like you.' Chou applied, tested, and was accepted. Captain Bruno was not what he expected—loud, confident, almost arrogant. But Bruno genuinely cared. 'Your kicks are good, but your footwork is sloppy,' Bruno said. 'You need to learn to read your opponent.' Chou trained harder. Bruno became his friend, his mentor, his brother. The polished captain and the rough brawler—unlikely, but perfect together.

chapters.title: Lancelot — The Noble Who Mocked Him
chapters.shortDesc: Chou met the noble knight Lancelot, who mocked his fashion sense. They became unlikely friends, and Lancelot helped Chou upgrade his wardrobe.
chapters.fullDesc: Lancelot was everything Chou despised—rich, privileged, beautiful. They met at a gala. 'So you are the famous Kung Fu Boy,' Lancelot said with a smirk. 'I had heard you were rough around the edges. I did not realise they meant literally.' Chou wanted to punch him. But he remembered Bruno's advice: sometimes protecting means swallowing your pride. He walked away. Lancelot followed and apologised. 'I was testing you. Most would have hit me. You walked away. That takes more strength.' They became unlikely friends. Lancelot's greatest contribution was fashion. 'You look like a walking warning sign,' he said of Chou's jumpsuit. He took Chou shopping, taught him about cuts and fabrics. Chou kept the jumpsuit—it was comfortable, and the 'BANG BANG' made him smile. Lancelot sighed, 'Some people cannot be saved.' But he was smiling too.

chapters.title: The Hero of the Streets
chapters.shortDesc: Chou returns to Antoinerei to help, wins a martial arts tournament, and decides his legacy: to keep fighting for the forgotten.
chapters.fullDesc: Chou returns to Antoinerei whenever he can. He funds schools, clinics, shelters. The people remember him as the boy who shared his food. They call him the Hero of the Slums. He does not like the title—he is just a man who got lucky. But he does what he can. The martial arts tournament in the capital drew fighters from across the empire. Chou entered on a whim. He faced masters, champions, warriors. In the final match, he faced a monk from the Monastery of Light. The fight lasted nearly an hour. In the end, Chou won with a single kick. The crowd chanted his name. He felt pride—not arrogant, but quiet and steady. He knew then that his legacy would not be trophies or titles. It would be the fights he fought for those who could not fight for themselves. He is Chou, the Kung Fu Boy. And he is still kicking.

chapters.title: The Foot That Keeps Kicking
chapters.shortDesc: Chou stands on a rooftop in Eruditio, watching over the city. He does not know what the future holds, but he will keep fighting.
chapters.fullDesc: "They call me the Kung Fu Boy. I did not choose the name. I did not want it. But I have carried it for many years now, and I have learned that names are just words. What matters is what you do. And what I do is fight. That is enough." — Chou, to a young boy in Antoinerei who asked him how to become a hero. The night is warm over Eruditio, the stars bright. Chou stands on the roof of the Rangers' headquarters, his eyes fixed on the horizon. The city is quiet, peaceful. He thinks about the slums, the monk, Lancelot, Bruno. He does not know what tomorrow will bring. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will fight. He will protect. He will kick. The foot never stops. And as long as Chou draws breath, there will be someone standing between the darkness and the light.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Chou's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Jeet Kune Do, Shunpo, The Way of the Dragon, and the Street Fighter's aura.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: rooted in his body—speed, precision, and relentless determination. No magic, no cybernetics. Only flesh, bone, and will.

Jeet Kune Do (Passive): the Way of the Intercepting Fist—strike first, strike fast, strike without warning.

Shunpo: a burst of speed that appears as teleportation, closing distance instantly.

The Way of the Dragon (Ultimate): a legendary combo—flurry of kicks, launching uppercut kick, spinning heel kick that sends enemies flying.

The Aura of the Street Fighter (Passive): a crackling intensity that energises allies and intimidates enemies.

chapters.title: On the Kung Fu Boy
