She returned from Mirror Lake, reborn as a mortal, and reclaimed her throne. She is not a hero. She will never be a hero. But she is not a villain. She is a ruler, a protector, a survivor. She will keep fighting, protecting, building a world where the outcasts belong. She will be the Phoenix Empress—not because she was born to it, but because she earned the right. Because someone must stand against the darkness. And Zetian, the nameless orphan who became the Phoenix Empress, has decided that someone will be her. The fire of the phoenix will never die.

chapters.title: The Dance of the Crimson Promise
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara introduces herself as the Fallen Scarlet, a geisha ninja who owes a life debt to Hanabi. She walked through hell to claim the Ukifune twin fans and now serves as Hanabi's shadow, protector, and weapon.
chapters.fullDesc: "A blade does not ask why it must cut. A shadow does not question where it must fall. A debt of life cannot be weighed against gold or measured in years. I was nothing—a forgotten girl shivering in the gutters of the Scarlet Shadow, my hands empty, my spirit broken, my heart hollow. Then she found me. Hanabi—the Scarlet Flower—saved me from a death that should have claimed me. She did not ask for my gratitude. She did not demand my service. She simply... saw me. And in that moment, I understood that there are debts that cannot be repaid with coin. There is only one currency that can balance the ledger of a life saved. Blood. I will bleed for her. I will kill for her. I will walk through the fires of the Abyss and return with nothing but ash on my skin if it means she never has to suffer. They call me the Fallen Scarlet now. They say I am a monster, a killer, a weapon with no soul. They are wrong. I have a soul. It is not mine. It belongs to her." — Hirara, speaking to the embers of a dying fire, her twin fans still wet with the blood of her enemies. She was found half-dead on the outskirts of the Scarlet Shadow's territory. Hanabi saved her. Now Hirara is her shadow, her protector, her Obsidian Dancer—and she will never stop dancing.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Gutter
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara was an orphan, forgotten and alone, until Hanabi found her dying in the mud. Hanabi gave her a name, a purpose, and a debt that could never be repaid.
chapters.fullDesc: The Cadia Riverlands do not remember the forgotten. Hirara was one of them—no parents, no home, no name. She survived by stealing and lying, learning that trust was weakness. At eight years old, she stumbled into the Scarlet Shadow's territory, half-dead, covered in wounds. The scouts wanted to kill her. But Hanabi, the grandmaster's daughter, intervened. 'She is a person,' Hanabi said. 'I will take responsibility for her.' She knelt in the mud, lifted the girl's head into her lap, poured water through cracked lips, and stayed for three days until the fever broke. 'What is your name?' she asked. The girl could not speak. 'It doesn't matter,' Hanabi said. 'I will give you a new name. Hirara. It means "the falling scarlet." You are not dead yet. You will not die today.' The debt was forged in that moment. Hirara would repay it with blood.

chapters.title: The Shadow That Learned to Strike
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara trained in secret, watching Scarlet warriors, adapting their techniques. She became Hanabi's bodyguard and killed her first assassin at fourteen, her hands wet with blood, her eyes cold.
chapters.fullDesc: Hanabi gave Hirara a purpose: 'You will be my bodyguard. You will stay by my side, watch my back, and keep me safe.' Hirara had no formal training, no bloodline, no talent—only hunger and loyalty. She watched the Scarlet warriors, memorized their forms, adapted their techniques. Her body became a weapon; her will became steel. The day she first killed for Hanabi, she was fourteen. An assassin infiltrated the compound. Hirara heard the whisper of fabric, felt the shift in air. She caught his wrist, twisted, took his dagger, and plunged it into his throat. The blood was warm on her hands. She did not vomit or weep. She simply stood, waiting for the next threat. Hanabi woke to the sound of the body collapsing. She looked at Hirara—at the blood, the cold resolve—and nodded. 'Good.' That was all.

chapters.title: The Debt That Could Not Be Weighed
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara became Hanabi's shadow, known among the Scarlet Shadow as the silent guardian who never failed. When Hanabi hunted Hanzo alone, Hirara followed and saved her.
chapters.fullDesc: The years passed. Hirara became known as Hanabi's shadow—the silent guardian who struck without warning, who asked no questions, who never failed. She was not a formal member of the clan. She had no insignia, no rituals. She was simply Hirara, and her only purpose was to protect Hanabi. Then came the betrayal of Hanzo. The Akuma Ninja had fallen to the cursed blade Ame no Habakiri. Hanabi was sent to hunt him alone, slipping away in the night to keep Hirara safe. Hirara woke to an empty room. She followed the trail of rumours, tracked Hanabi into the Shadow Swamp. She found Hanabi fighting Hanzo—wounded, exhausted, losing. Hirara threw herself into the fight, drew Hanzo's attention, and gave Hanabi the opening she needed. Together, they drove him back. Hanabi was furious. 'You could have died.' 'So could you,' Hirara replied. 'I made a promise. I will not let you die. Not ever.' The debt had been repaid a hundred times over. But Hirara did not keep count.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Geisha Ninja
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Hirara: 160 cm, slender and athletic, teal-blue hair in a complex updo, vivid pinkish-purple eyes, porcelain skin, asymmetrical combat gear, wooden geta, and the twin fans Ukifune.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Hirara is to see a contradiction made physical—a woman who moves like a dancer, fights like a demon, and carries herself with the poise of a geisha even as her fans drip with blood. She stands 160 centimetres, slender and athletic. Her face is sharp and refined, with a V-shaped jawline and high cheekbones. Her skin is porcelain white, her eyes large and vivid pinkish-purple, framed by dark eyeliner. Her hair is deep teal-blue, styled in a complex updo with thick bangs and a spiky bun. She wears a white sarashi under a dark charcoal cropped vest with gold embroidery. Her arms are asymmetrically armoured—an ornate gauntlet on the right, a dark sleeve with gold bands on the left. A thick red sash with a blue floral charm and red tassels cinches her waist, from which flare teal fan-like panels. A short dark skirt exposes her thighs, wrapped in white bandages on the right leg. Her left leg is bare; her right leg wears a thigh-high black stocking with red flame lines. On her feet are black geta with red straps. Her weapons are the Ukifune—Kaerazu (crimson fire fan) and Meisen-e (magenta shadow fan). Her aura is cold, contained fury—the presence of a woman who has learned to move through the world without leaving a trace.

chapters.title: The Twin Fans of Ukifune
chapters.shortDesc: The Ukifune are legendary twin fans of the Scarlet Shadow. Hirara claimed them by walking through a forbidden ritual, proving her obsession stronger than the spirits bound within.
chapters.fullDesc: The Ukifune are part of the Seven Great Armaments, ancient relics sealed in the Scarlet Shadow's vaults. To claim them, Hirara walked into a forbidden ritual—a hell that should have killed her. The spirits tested not strength, but obsession. They showed her illusions of her past: cold nights, empty stomachs, people who looked through her. They whispered that she was nothing, that Hanabi would forget her. Hirara fought for three days. Her body broke. Her spirit exhausted. Then she remembered Hanabi—the girl who knelt in the mud, who poured water through cracked lips, who saw a dying stray and found something worth saving. She rose. The spirits recoiled. Her obsession was too pure, too absolute. She emerged with the Ukifune in her hands—Kaerazu, the Crimson Bringer, and Meisen-e, the Shadow Weaver. Hanabi watched from the shadows. 'You are no longer my shadow,' she said. 'You are my equal.' 'I am your protector,' Hirara replied. 'That is all I have ever wanted to be.'

chapters.title: The Abilities of the Fallen Scarlet
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara's combat style: Twin Fans passive, Kaerazu (fan-shaped damage), Meisen-e (double dash), Infernal Torrent (dash spin combo), Falling Maple (untargetable phase), and Momijigari (energy-extending ultimate).
chapters.fullDesc: Hirara's power is defined by pressure and combo chaining. Twin Fans: Ukifune (Passive)—she wields Kaerazu and Meisen-e. She starts with 4 Crimson/Death Energy stacks. Casting base skills costs 1 energy, combos cost 2. CDR converts to energy recovery. Hitting with both marks immobilises enemies. Kaerazu (Skill 1)—sweeps a fan-shaped attack, dealing damage, then a delayed second strike for double damage. Meisen-e (Skill 2)—dashes twice, slicing enemies, then releases a water wave. Infernal Torrent (Combo 1→2)—dashes forward spinning, deals damage, then spins again for double damage in a wide circle. Falling Maple (Combo 2→1)—becomes untargetable for up to 1 second, then emerges with an AoE sweep and two free dashes. Forbidden Jutsu: Momijigari (Ultimate)—gains burst movement speed, increases max energy to 6 stacks for 10 seconds; each kill or assist extends duration by 4 seconds, enabling snowball combos.

chapters.title: The Walk Through Fire
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara's forbidden ritual to claim the Ukifune nearly killed her, but her obsession with protecting Hanabi proved stronger than the spirits of the dead.
chapters.fullDesc: The ritual was forbidden, sealed in the oldest texts. It required a sacrifice not of blood, but of self—to face the spirits bound within the Great Armaments and prove that one's will was stronger than the collective hunger of the dead. The elders warned Hirara she would die. Hanabi did not try to stop her. 'You will die,' Hanabi said. 'Perhaps,' Hirara replied. 'But if I live, I will be strong enough to protect you. That is all that matters.' She stepped into the vault, and darkness swallowed her. For three days she fought spirits who tried to consume her identity, who whispered she was nothing. She fought until she could not remember who she was. Then she remembered Hanabi. She rose. The spirits recoiled. She emerged scarred, her hair turned white in places, her soul permanently changed—but alive, with the Ukifune in her hands. The elders bowed. The warriors whispered her name with new respect. Hanabi smiled.

chapters.title: The Obsidian Dancer and the Web of Duty
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara faced Hanzo again, using Falling Maple to phase through his attacks and Infernal Torrent to drive him back. She swore to follow Hanabi into darkness if needed.
chapters.fullDesc: The Cadia Riverlands are a web of alliances and betrayals. When the Abyss sent agents to corrupt the Scarlet Shadow, Hirara fought them in the shadows. When Hanzo returned, drawn by old grudges, Hirara stood between him and Hanabi. Hanzo laughed. 'You cannot protect her. The darkness will take her.' 'Then I will follow her into the darkness,' Hirara replied, 'and I will drag her back.' She attacked. She used Falling Maple to phase through his claws, to dodge his most devastating strikes. She used Infernal Torrent to close the distance, to deliver blows even he could not ignore. Hanzo retreated, wounded and furious. He would return. He always returned. Hirara did not care. She would be ready. She would keep dancing.

chapters.title: The Heart That Never Yielded
chapters.shortDesc: Years of vigilance left Hirara scarred and lonely. She loved Hanabi with a fierceness she could not name, but she accepted her role as the shadow, the weapon, the protector.
chapters.fullDesc: The years took their toll. Hirara's body was a map of scars, her mind a fortress of secrets, her heart a vault sealed shut. She did not sleep well—the spirits of the Ukifune whispered to her in the dark, urging violence. But she did not lose herself. Hanabi needed her. The Scarlet Shadow needed her. She trained harder, refined her techniques, became a legend—the Fallen Scarlet, the Obsidian Dancer. But she was lonely. The bond with Hanabi was deeper than friendship, but also more distant. Hanabi was her mistress, her purpose, not her equal. She had no one to confide in, no one to hold her when nightmares came. She did not complain. She had chosen this path. She would walk it to the end. 'Every slash is a prayer for the safety of my master.'

chapters.title: The Philosophy of the Fallen Scarlet
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara's philosophy: a blade does not ask why it must cut. She believes in loyalty, sacrifice, and the art of battle. She has accepted her role and does not resent it.
chapters.fullDesc: Hirara does not consider herself a philosopher. She thinks about the next threat, the next battle. But she has developed guiding beliefs. 'A blade does not ask why it must cut. A shadow does not question where it must fall.' She has accepted her role. She believes in loyalty—not blind loyalty, but the deep abiding loyalty of a life to the one who saved it. She owes Hanabi everything, and she will pay that debt for as long as she lives. She believes in sacrifice. She walked through hell, gave everything—her body, her soul, her future—to a single woman. She does not regret it. 'Dancing on a battlefield is the greatest art. It is the only art that matters.'

chapters.title: The Bond with the Fallen Flower
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara loves Hanabi with a devotion that transcends duty. Hanabi once said, 'You are not my shadow. You are my heart.' Hirara has never forgotten those words.
chapters.fullDesc: The most important bond in Hirara's life is with Hanabi. She is not Hanabi's friend—friends are equals. She is her protector, her shadow, her weapon. But there is love there—a love never spoken, never acknowledged, but always present. Hirara loves Hanabi with a fierceness she cannot name, a devotion that transcends duty, that goes beyond obligation. Hanabi knows. She does not speak of it, because she cannot offer what Hirara deserves. She is bound to Hayabusa, to her clan, to a destiny that has no room for a shadow. But she has never asked Hirara to leave. 'You are not my shadow,' Hanabi once said. 'You are my heart.' Hirara did not reply. She could not. But she remembered the words. She has never forgotten them.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Obsidian Dancer
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara does not know if she will ever find peace, but she will keep dancing, keep protecting, keep fighting. She is the Fallen Scarlet, and she will never stop.
chapters.fullDesc: Hirara does not know what the future holds. She does not know if she will ever find peace, if the Ukifune will ever release her, if the debt she owes will ever be paid in full. But she knows she will keep fighting, protecting, dancing on the edge of the blade for as long as her body allows. She was born in the gutter, forgotten and alone. She was saved by a girl who saw something no one else could see. She walked through hell to claim her power. She is not a hero. She will never be a hero. But she is not a villain. She is a guardian, a protector, a weapon. She is Hirara, the Fallen Scarlet. And she will never stop dancing.

chapters.title: The Dance That Never Ends
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara stands vigil at the Scarlet Shadow's compound, watching over the night. She thinks of Hanabi, the girl in the gutter, and the Ukifune. She keeps dancing.
chapters.fullDesc: "Dancing on a battlefield is the greatest art. Every slash is a prayer for the safety of my master." — Hirara, standing on the edge of the Scarlet Shadow's compound, her fans raised, her eyes fixed on the horizon. The night is quiet. The moon hangs low. Hirara stands at the edge of the compound, fans in her hands, eyes fixed on the horizon. In the distance, village lights twinkle—people sleeping peacefully, unaware of the woman who watches from the shadows. It is worth it. Every scar, every battle, every sacrifice. She thinks of the girl in the gutter, hoping she is proud. She thinks of Hanabi, hoping she is safe and happy. She thinks of the Ukifune, wondering how much longer she can carry them. 'Dancing on a battlefield is the greatest art,' she whispers. The wind does not answer, but the stars shine brighter. She is not alone. Hanabi is with her, the Ukifune are with her, the memory of the girl in the gutter is with her. The night is quiet. The moon is silver. And Hirara, the Fallen Scarlet, keeps her vigil.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Hirara's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Twin Fans passive, Kaerazu, Meisen-e, Infernal Torrent, Falling Maple, and Momijigari. Hirara is a high-mobility assassin who chains combos with unique drag-and-drop mechanics.
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of Her Power: earned through a forbidden ritual, focused through the Ukifune twin fans. She operates on Crimson/Death Energy instead of mana or standard cooldowns.

Twin Fans: Ukifune (Passive): wields Kaerazu and Meisen-e. Starts with 4 energy stacks. Base skills cost 1 energy, combos cost 2. CDR converts to energy recovery. Hitting with both marks immobilises enemies for 0.8s.

Kaerazu (Skill 1): sweeps a fan-shaped attack, deals damage, then a delayed second strike for double damage.

Meisen-e (Skill 2): dashes twice, slicing enemies, then releases a water wave.

Infernal Torrent (Combo 1→2): dashes forward spinning, deals damage, then spins again for double damage in a wide circle. Primary kill combo.

Falling Maple (Combo 2→1): becomes untargetable for up to 1 second, then emerges with AoE sweep and two free dashes. Ultimate outplay tool.

Forbidden Jutsu: Momijigari (Ultimate): gains burst movement speed, increases max energy to 6 stacks for 10 seconds. Kills/assists extend duration by 4 seconds. Snowball tool for teamfight dominance.

chapters.title: On the Fallen Scarlet
chapters.shortDesc: Hirara will be the Fallen Scarlet not because she was born to it, but because she chose to dance through hell for a promise made in blood. She will never stop dancing.
chapters.fullDesc: Hirara. Fallen Scarlet. Obsidian Dancer. She was born in the gutter, an orphan with no name, no home, no future. She was saved by a girl who saw something no one else could see. She became her shadow, her protector, her weapon. She walked through a hell that should have killed her to claim the Ukifune. She is not a hero. She will never be a hero. But she is not a villain. She is a guardian, a protector, a weapon. She will keep dancing, keep protecting, keep fighting. She will be the Fallen Scarlet—not because she was born to it, but because she chose to dance through hell for a promise made in blood. Because someone must stand in the shadows and watch over the ones who matter. And Hirara, the girl from the gutter, the shadow of the Scarlet Flower, the Obsidian Dancer, has decided that someone will be her. She will never stop dancing.

chapters.title: The Scale That Devours Memory
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong introduces himself as the Black Dragon, a nameless orphan who rose to become a calamity. He stole the forbidden Reverse Scale, plunged it into his chest, and devoured the ancient Black Dragon's consciousness to claim its power.
chapters.fullDesc: "They say I was a monster long before I became one. They say the Black Dragon chose me because it recognised its own kind—a soul already twisted by ambition, already hollowed out by hunger. They are not wrong. I cannot remember a time when the desire for power did not burn within me. I was an orphan of the Cadia Riverlands, a feral child who survived on the outskirts of civilisation through cunning and an unbreakable will. I had nothing. I was nothing. But I wanted everything. The Great Dragon saw something in me—or so he claimed. He took me in, fed me, clothed me, trained me. He called me his disciple. He taught me that balance was the highest virtue, that harmony was the greatest good. He was wrong. Balance is stagnation. Harmony is submission. I wanted to be free. I wanted to be strong. I wanted to reshape the world in my own image. The Reverse Scale whispered to me from its prison, promising the power to overthrow the stagnant order of the heavens. I listened. I stole the Scale. I plunged it into my own chest. The ancient Black Dragon tried to devour me, to claim my consciousness as its own. But I was not a vessel. I was a rival. I devoured it instead. Now I am the Black Dragon. I am the calamity that will burn away the old order and forge a new one from the ashes. I am Yu Zhong, the Black Dragon. And I will never bow again."

chapters.title: The Feral Child of the Cadia Riverlands
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong was a nameless orphan, surviving on the outskirts of civilisation through theft and violence. He had nothing and no one, but his fierce, defiant eyes caught the attention of the Great Dragon.
chapters.fullDesc: The Cadia Riverlands were vast and beautiful, but they had a shadow side. Yu Zhong was one of the forgotten—no parents, no home, no future. He survived by stealing food, sleeping in doorways, fighting other strays over scraps. He learned that the world was cruel, that kindness was weakness, that the only way to survive was to be stronger than everyone else. An old woman once said, 'You have the eyes of a predator. The same eyes as the Black Dragon, before the Great Dragon sealed him.' Yu Zhong did not know who the Black Dragon was. He only knew that he was hungry, and he would not let anyone stand in his way. Then the Great Dragon found him in a back alley, watching him fight off a group of thugs. The boy was outnumbered, bleeding, but he did not run. The Great Dragon stepped from the shadows: 'You have potential. Come with me. I will teach you.' Yu Zhong followed.

chapters.title: The Disciple of the Dragon Altar
chapters.shortDesc: The Great Dragon took Yu Zhong to the Dragon Altar, a place of discipline and meditation. Yu Zhong struggled at first, but he trained alongside Zilong and Baxia, growing stronger with each passing day.
chapters.fullDesc: The Dragon Altar demanded discipline, meditation, and rigorous training. Yu Zhong struggled—he was not used to stillness or trust. The other disciples looked at him with suspicion, sensing the wildness beneath his skin. But the Great Dragon assigned him to train alongside Zilong, the most promising disciple of his generation. Zilong was everything Yu Zhong was not: patient, humble, devoted to the cause. Their training sessions were brutal. Yu Zhong pushed himself harder than anyone else, desperate to prove his worth. He learned the spear, the sword, the art of combat. He learned to channel his inner energy, to calm his restless spirit. But beneath the surface, a hunger gnawed at him. 'You are growing stronger,' Zilong said. 'I am not strong enough,' Yu Zhong replied. 'My anger is what drives me. Without it, I am nothing.' Zilong did not understand. The rift between them began to grow.

chapters.title: The Training of the Prodigy
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong became the most brilliant disciple of his generation, but he chafed against the Great Dragon's philosophy of balance. He believed the strong should rule and that chaos was the only true path to evolution.
chapters.fullDesc: Yu Zhong mastered every technique the Dragon Altar offered. He surpassed his fellow disciples, earned the grudging respect of his masters, and became friends with Zilong and Baxia. He trained alongside Luo Yi, the geomancer who would later become his most loyal strategist. But the deeper he delved into the Great Dragon's teachings, the more a hunger gnawed at his soul. He perceived the philosophy of 'balance' not as wisdom, but as a cage—a deliberate suppression of the strong to coddle the weak. 'The world is meant to be ruled by the powerful,' he told Zilong. 'Harmony is submission. Chaos is evolution.' Zilong warned him against such heretical thoughts. Yu Zhong did not listen. His ambition festered, waiting for the moment to ignite.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Knowledge
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong discovered the Reverse Scale—a shard of draconic power from the primordial Black Dragon—sealed in the Forbidden Area beneath the Dragon Altar. It whispered to him, promising the power to overthrow the heavens.
chapters.fullDesc: The Reverse Scale was the most closely guarded secret of the Dragon Altar—a shard of draconic power, the last remnant of the primordial Black Dragon that the Great Dragon had vanquished eons ago. Yu Zhong found it by accident while exploring the lower levels. The Scale floated in a field of golden light, pulsing with dark, rhythmic energy. 'You are the one,' a voice whispered. 'The one who will break the chains. The one who will free me.' Yu Zhong did not know if the voice was real. He did not care. 'How?' he whispered. 'Take me. Let me into your heart. Let me become part of you. Together, we will reshape the world.' Yu Zhong reached for the Scale. His fingers brushed its surface. The energy surged.

chapters.title: The Hunger Within
chapters.shortDesc: The Reverse Scale awakened something within Yu Zhong. His skin darkened, his eyes glowed red, and scales grew on his body. Zilong confronted him, but Yu Zhong stormed out of the Dragon Altar, vowing never to return.
chapters.fullDesc: The Reverse Scale did not corrupt Yu Zhong—it awakened something that had always been there. He began to change: his skin grew darker, his eyes glowed with faint red light, his body developed shimmering obsidian scales. The other disciples whispered, afraid of the monster growing in their midst. Zilong confronted him. 'What is happening to you?' 'I am becoming what I was meant to be.' 'You are becoming a monster. The Great Dragon can help you.' 'I do not need help. I need power.' Words were exchanged that could not be taken back. Zilong accused Yu Zhong of betrayal. Yu Zhong accused Zilong of cowardice. 'The Great Dragon does not keep us weak. He teaches us to find strength in harmony.' 'Harmony is submission. I will not bow to anyone.' He stormed out of the Altar that night, vowing never to return.

chapters.title: The Wanderer's Path
chapters.shortDesc: For years, Yu Zhong wandered the Land of Dawn, challenging powerful warriors and growing stronger. Then he met Luo Yi, who revealed that he was the reincarnation of the Black Dragon.
chapters.fullDesc: For years, Yu Zhong wandered through the Moniyan Empire, the Agelta Drylands, the Barren Lands. He sought out powerful warriors, challenged them to duels, absorbed their strength. He grew stronger with each battle, but he lacked purpose. Then he met Luo Yi. She found him collapsed in the desert, the Reverse Scale devouring him, the ancient Black Dragon's consciousness fighting for control. She did not fear him. 'You are the one. The reincarnation of the Black Dragon. I have been waiting for you.' She nursed him back to health, taught him to control the Scale's power, and revealed the truth: he was the ancient enemy of the Great Dragon, the champion of chaos. 'You have a choice. Continue wandering, nameless and purposeless. Or embrace your destiny. Become the Black Dragon. Reshape the Cadia Riverlands in your own image.' Yu Zhong looked at his trembling hands—not with fear, but with anticipation. 'It is time to stop running.'

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Calamity
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Yu Zhong: tall and imposing, sharp angular jaw, glowing red eyes, smoky charcoal hair, black goatee, armour with glowing red chest seam, dragon-headed pauldron, scale cape, red horns, and his terrifying Black Dragon form.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Yu Zhong is to see a being caught between two worlds. He stands tall with a lean, powerful physique. His face is sharp and angular, with high cheekbones and a straight, noble nose. His eyes glow with piercing red light, framed by eyebrows that angle upward like dragon horns. A dark mark lies between his brows. His hair is smoky charcoal, swept back, with a neat dark goatee. His upper body wears interlocking plate armour of gunmetal silver and deep violet, with a glowing red vertical seam on his chest. A segmented gauntlet with talons covers his right arm; his left shoulder bears a massive pauldron shaped like a dragon's head with a glowing red eye. A heavy cape of overlapping purple and lavender scales flows from his left shoulder, its edges tattered with silver spikes. His lower body is protected by heavy greaves and armoured sabatons. Two glowing red horns emerge from his temples, curving backward. In his Black Dragon form, he becomes a colossal serpentine dragon of shadow and fire, his scales gleaming like obsidian, his wings blotting out the sun. His aura is oppressive, suffocating—the presence of a primordial calamity.

chapters.title: Cursing Touch — The Hunger That Feeds
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong's passive ability applies Sha Residue with each hit. At five stacks, the residue erupts, dealing damage based on missing HP, healing Yu Zhong, and granting movement speed and spell vamp.
chapters.fullDesc: Cursing Touch is Yu Zhong's passive ability—the manifestation of the Reverse Scale's hunger. Every time he deals damage, he applies Sha Residue, stacking up to five times. At five stacks, the residue erupts, consuming one stack every half-second. Each eruption deals 40 (+30% Extra Physical Attack) + 2% of the target's lost HP as physical damage, restores 8% of his lost HP, and increases his movement speed. When fully charged, Sha Essence grants him 40% movement speed and 20% spell vamp. The ability rewards aggression: the more he fights, the more he heals. It favours one-on-one situations but also makes him formidable in crowded team fights. 'Your pain is my pleasure,' Yu Zhong says, as the Sha Residue erupts. He embraces the chaos, turning every wound into fuel for his relentless advance.

chapters.title: Dragon Tail, Soul Grip, and Furious Dive — The Tools of Destruction
chapters.shortDesc: Dragon Tail spins his cloak for area damage. Soul Grip launches a draconic claw that slows and knocks back. Furious Dive dashes twice and knocks enemies airborne. These skills build Sha Residue and enable his ultimate.
chapters.fullDesc: Dragon Tail (Skill 1) infuses his power into his cloak, causing it to spin after a short delay. The inner area deals 200-380 physical damage; the sharpened edge deals 250% damage and applies two stacks of Sha Residue. Max this skill first for its low cooldown and high damage. Soul Grip (Skill 2) unleashes the Dragon Soul, dealing 150-225 physical damage in a line, slowing enemies by 60% for one second, and enhancing his next basic attack to knock back the target. Hitting multiple targets applies Sha Residue multiple times. This is his primary engage tool. Furious Dive (Skill 3) leaps to a designated area, dealing 180-270 physical damage, then allows a second dash. After a short delay, enemies in the area are knocked airborne and take additional damage. This is his best crowd-control skill, ideal for chasing or dodging. Together, these techniques build Sha Residue, set up his ultimate, and turn him into a whirlwind of destruction.

chapters.title: The Return to the Dragon Altar
chapters.shortDesc: Years after his exile, Yu Zhong returned to the Dragon Altar as the Black Dragon, leading an army of the discontented. He fought Zilong, Baxia, and Ling, broke the seal, and merged fully with the Reverse Scale.
chapters.fullDesc: Yu Zhong returned to the Dragon Altar with his army of followers. Zilong met him at the gates with Baxia and Ling. 'You should not have come back.' 'I was never gone. The time has come for change.' 'Change is not destruction.' 'Destruction is the only change that matters.' They fought. Zilong was stronger than Yu Zhong remembered; Baxia's shell absorbed blow after blow; Ling's blade struck from unexpected angles. But Yu Zhong had the power of the Reverse Scale. He drove them back, reached the Forbidden Area, and broke the seal. The Scale merged fully with his body. He became the complete Black Dragon. 'You have lost. The old order is dead. A new one will rise from its ashes.' Zilong struggled to his feet. 'The Great Dragon's teachings will never die.' Yu Zhong laughed coldly, transformed into his draconic form, and flew into the sky, his wings blotting out the sun.

chapters.title: The Strategist's Gambit
chapters.shortDesc: Luo Yi had planned for Yu Zhong's rise, but she also harboured her own vision for the world. She warned him that she served only as long as their goals aligned, and watched him from the shadows.
chapters.fullDesc: Luo Yi had known that Yu Zhong would return, break the seal, and become the Black Dragon. She had gathered intelligence, forged alliances, positioned her pieces. But she also hidden her own vision—a world that might not align with Yu Zhong's. 'Do not trust me,' she told him, as they stood on a mountain peak. 'I serve you because our goals align. When they diverge, I will follow my own path.' Yu Zhong's red eyes were unreadable. 'I do not expect loyalty. I expect competence. As long as you provide it, you will have a place at my side.' Luo Yi inclined her head. 'That is all I ask.' She had found the reincarnated Black Dragon, helped him gather strength, and prepared for a comeback. But she was also watching, waiting, planning. The Black Dragon was not the only one with ambition.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Black Dragon
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong does not know if he will succeed in crushing the Dragon Altar, but he will keep conquering. He is the Black Dragon—the calamity that will burn away the old order and forge a new world from ashes.
chapters.fullDesc: Yu Zhong does not know what the future holds. He does not know if he will succeed in crushing the Dragon Altar, if Luo Yi will betray him, if the Reverse Scale will eventually consume him. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will conquer. He will destroy. He will rebuild. The hunger never stops. The flames never die. The dragon never rests. He was a nameless orphan who had nothing. He became a disciple who had everything. He chose to embrace the monster within. Now he is the Black Dragon, the reincarnation of an ancient evil, the calamity that will burn away the old order. He will keep fighting for the world that he believes should be his. And he will never stop conquering.

chapters.title: The Fire That Burns Forever
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong stands on a peak overlooking the Dragon Altar, his wings spread, his eyes fixed on the distant lights. The battle is coming, and he is ready. He will never stop.
chapters.fullDesc: "They call me the Black Dragon. I did not choose the name. I do not care about names. I care about power—the endless, intoxicating, eternal power that flows through the Reverse Scale and transforms me into something greater than a man. I am Yu Zhong. I am the reincarnation of an ancient evil. I am the calamity that will burn away the old order. And I will never stop." — Yu Zhong, standing on the peak of a mountain, his wings spread, his eyes fixed on the Dragon Altar below. The night is dark over the Cadia Riverlands. Yu Zhong stands on a peak, his draconic wings folded, his eyes fixed on the distant lights of the Dragon Altar. The disciples are preparing. The Great Dragon is watching. The battle is coming. He thinks about the stray who had nothing, the disciple who had everything, the monster who chose to embrace his nature. He does not know if the hunger will ever end. But he knows what he will do: conquer, destroy, rebuild. The wings wait. The fire burns. The dragon is ready. And as long as Yu Zhong draws breath, there will be someone fighting to reshape the Cadia Riverlands in flames and shadow.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Yu Zhong's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Cursing Touch (Sha Residue), Dragon Tail (cloak spin), Soul Grip (claw slow/knockback), Furious Dive (dash knock-up), and Black Dragon Form (ultimate CC immunity and transformation).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: rooted in the Reverse Scale, fused with his body through will and hunger. He devoured the ancient Black Dragon's consciousness and claimed its power.

Cursing Touch (Passive): each hit applies Sha Residue (max 5 stacks). At 5 stacks, residue erupts every 0.5s, dealing 40 (+30% Extra Physical Attack) + 2% target's lost HP damage, restoring 8% lost HP, and increasing movement speed. At full charge, gains 40% movement speed and 20% spell vamp.

Dragon Tail (Skill 1): after a short delay, spins his cloak, dealing 200-380 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage. Outer area deals 250% damage and applies 2 Sha stacks. Cooldown 6-4.5s.

Soul Grip (Skill 2): unleashes a line attack dealing 150-225 (+120% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage, slowing by 60% for 1s, then enhanced basic attack knocks back enemies. Cooldown 12s.

Furious Dive (Skill 3): leaps twice, dealing 180-270 (+90% Extra Physical Attack) damage per dash; after a short delay, knocks enemies airborne and deals additional damage.

Black Dragon Form (Ultimate): transforms into a colossal dragon for up to 17s, gaining CC immunity, HP increase, and collision knockback (once per target).

The Aura of the Black Dragon: oppressive, suffocating, terrifying—the presence of a primordial calamity that makes allies feel empowered and enemies feel doomed.

chapters.title: On the Black Dragon
chapters.shortDesc: Yu Zhong will be the Black Dragon not because he was born to it, but because he chose to tear down the old order. He will keep conquering, burning, and remaking the world in his image.
chapters.fullDesc: Black Dragon. The title is a burden and a gift. It reminds Yu Zhong of the stray who had nothing, the disciple who had everything, the monster he chose to become. He does not know if he will ever be worthy of the title or live up to its expectations. But he knows he will try. Every day, in every battle, with every eruption. He will be strong, ruthless, unstoppable. He will be the Black Dragon. Not because he wants to be. Because he has to be. Because someone has to tear down the old order. And Yu Zhong, the nameless orphan, the prodigal disciple, the reincarnation of an ancient evil, has decided that someone will be him. The night is dark. The flames burn. The dragon waits. And Yu Zhong never stops conquering.

chapters.title: The Scar That Never Fades
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn introduces himself as the Rogue Appraiser, a treasure hunter carrying a crystal in his chest—a gift from his dying best friend Fray. He searches for Fray's ghost across Los Pecados, never stopping, never giving up.
chapters.fullDesc: "They say I am a money-grubber. A treasure-hungry scavenger who would trade his own mother for a fistful of gold. They whisper that I killed my best friend for a magical crystal—that I stabbed him in the back, ripped the gem from his chest, and sewed it into my own flesh to steal his power. They are wrong about everything except the scar. The scar on my chest is real. It is jagged, ugly, a violent tear in my flesh that I never bothered to hide. The crystal beneath it has long since merged with my heart, pulsing with an energy that is not entirely my own. I did not steal this crystal. It was given to me—pressed into my hands by a dying man who smiled even as the light faded from his eyes. His name was Fray. He was my best friend, my brother in everything but blood. We met on the road, two runaways from worlds that had tried to cage us. He was a scholar fleeing a temple that demanded too much. I was a noble fleeing a family that expected too little. We had nothing in common except our hunger for adventure and our refusal to be bound. He saved my life in a crumbling altar, and I have been trying to repay that debt ever since. The compass he left behind still spins, pointing toward something I cannot see. And the crystal in my chest hums with a rhythm that matches my heartbeat—a reminder that he is not gone, only waiting. I am Fredrinn, the Rogue Appraiser. I am the son of Duke Vance who chose freedom over fortune. I am the treasure hunter who has been searching for a ghost for more years than I care to count. And I will not stop until I find him. Not because I want to. Because I made a promise."

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn was born the eldest son of Archduke Waldo Vance, heir to Castle Grandrock. Raised without affection, trained in swordplay and diplomacy, he learned to suppress his emotions—until his father arranged a political marriage he refused.
chapters.fullDesc: Castle Grandrock was a monument to the Vance family's power—a fortress of grey stone and gleaming spires. Fredrinn was born in the highest tower. His father visited once a week, measuring his growth like a piece of property. 'He has potential,' the Archduke said. 'We will cultivate it.' His mother was a ghost, invisible to survive. Fredrinn was trained from age four in swordplay, from six in diplomacy, from ten in manipulation. His tutors were merciless. Failure was punished; success was expected. 'You are a Vance. You do not fail. You do not hesitate. You do not feel.' He learned to smile at people he despised, to laugh at jokes that were not funny, to bow to nobles who would have sold him. His half-sister Lesley was a cold markswoman; his younger brother Harley was a chaotic prodigy. Fredrinn loved them, but he could not stay.

chapters.title: The Engagement That Broke the Camel's Back
chapters.shortDesc: At a grand banquet, Archduke Vance announced Fredrinn's engagement to a woman he had never met. Fredrinn refused. His father gave him a choice: obey, or leave and be erased from the family records.
chapters.fullDesc: The announcement came during a banquet with roasted peacocks and imported wine. The Archduke declared that his eldest son would wed the daughter of a powerful southern house. Fredrinn had never met the woman. He excused himself. His father followed him into the corridor. 'You will do this.' 'I will not.' The argument lasted hours. Accusations were hurled, insults exchanged. In the end, the Archduke gave his son a choice: obey, or leave. 'If you walk out that door, you are no longer a Vance. Your name will be erased. Your siblings will be told you are dead. You will have nothing.' 'I already have nothing,' Fredrinn said. He walked out into the night.

chapters.title: The Wanderer's Road
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn wandered the Land of Dawn, surviving on his wits. A bar fight nearly killed him; a passing merchant saved him. He recovered and decided to become a treasure hunter, seeking adventure beyond the gilded halls of his past.
chapters.fullDesc: The first months were hardest. Fredrinn had grown up in luxury; now he fended for himself—sleeping in barns, eating stale bread, fighting with his hands. He travelled through the Moniyan Empire, the Cadia Riverlands, the Agelta Drylands. He saw poverty that made his childhood complaints absurd, kindness from strangers who had nothing, cruelty from those who had everything. A wound from a bar fight nearly killed him. He lay in a gutter for three days, feverish, alone. A passing merchant dragged him to a healer. He recovered slowly, losing weight and illusions—but gaining a hunger for adventure. He decided to become a treasure hunter.

chapters.title: The Meeting at the Crossroads
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn met Fray, a disgraced scholar with ink-stained fingers and a passion for ancient history. They became partners, then friends, then brothers in everything but blood.
chapters.fullDesc: Fredrinn met Fray at a crossroads in the Cadia Riverlands. Fray was sitting on a rock, studying a map older than the kingdoms it depicted. 'You are lost.' 'I am exactly where I need to be. The question is whether you are.' They travelled together for months. Fray was a former acolyte expelled for asking too many questions. He had ink-stained fingers, a disheveled appearance, and a mind that could decipher inscriptions that baffled the empire's finest scholars. He treated Fredrinn like an equal. They explored ruins, shared findings, argued about interpretations. Fray taught Fredrinn to read ancient scripts; Fredrinn taught Fray to fight. They became partners, then friends, then brothers in everything but blood.

chapters.title: The Altar and the Ritual
chapters.shortDesc: Following a rumour, Fredrinn and Fray entered an ancient altar in the Agelta Drylands. The ceiling collapsed. Fray pressed a glowing crystal into Fredrinn's hands and told him to go. Fredrinn woke outside alone.
chapters.fullDesc: A half-crazed traveller claimed to have seen an ancient altar in a dream. The description matched inscriptions Fray had decoded. The altar was buried beneath centuries of sand in the Agelta Drylands—a chamber of ritual where ancient mages performed ceremonies long dismissed as myth. Fredrinn and Fray entered together. The tunnels were dark, the traps deadly. They found the heart: a chamber filled with ghostly figures. The ritual was already in progress. The collapse began without warning. Stone shattered. Fray reached for a glowing crystal embedded in the altar's centre. 'Take it. It will lead you out.' 'Not without you.' The ceiling collapsed between them. When Fredrinn woke, he was outside, the crystal in his hand, Fray's compass beside him. Fray was gone.

chapters.title: The Compass That Never Points North
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn searched the rubble for days, finding nothing. The compass spun wildly, never pointing north. He stayed in Los Pecados, becoming a treasure appraiser to fund his search for Fray's ghost.
chapters.fullDesc: Fredrinn searched the rubble for days, digging with his bare hands, calling Fray's name until his throat was raw. He found nothing. The altar had swallowed his friend, leaving no trace. He sat on the rocks, the crystal warm against his chest, the compass spinning in his hand. 'He is not dead. He is missing. And I will find him.' The compass never pointed to a fixed direction, but sometimes the needle would quiver—pointing toward a distant ruin, a forgotten city, a place where clues might be hidden. Fredrinn stayed in Los Pecados, city of sin, where information was bought and sold. He became a treasure appraiser, a 'money-grubber,' accumulating wealth not for its own sake, but because wealth bought access to the network he needed.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Treasure Hunter
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Fredrinn: six feet tall, lean and powerful, tanned skin, piercing blue eyes, chestnut brown hair with a braid, scarred chest with a crystal, navy blue coat, and a massive rune-etched broadsword.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Fredrinn is to see a man shaped by freedom and scarred by loss. He stands over six feet, lean and powerful—dense muscle from years of climbing ruins and fighting monsters. His face has a strong jawline, high cheekbones, a straight nose. His skin is tanned, weathered by desert sun. His eyes are piercing blue—the colour of the sea at twilight, always searching. His hair is chestnut brown, swept back with a single braid over his shoulder. He dresses like a noble who forgot how to care: a long navy blue coat, embroidered with silver thread, stained and patched, hanging open over a white shirt and dark trousers. A thick leather belt holds pouches, a compass, a crystal, a dagger, a notebook. His hands are scarred, calloused, steady. His weapon is a massive broadsword, nearly as tall as he is, etched with runes that glow in the dark. The scar on his chest is jagged and ugly—a map of his past, a testament to his survival. The crystal beneath pulses with a rhythm that matches his heartbeat.

chapters.title: Crystalline Armour — The Heart That Remembers
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn's passive ability stores damage as Crystal Energy and converts dealt damage into healing. He gains Combo Points when hitting non-minion enemies, fueling his stronger skills.
chapters.fullDesc: Crystalline Armour is Fredrinn's passive—the manifestation of the crystal merged with his heart. He stores damage as Crystal Energy; every blow, arrow, spell is absorbed and held. The energy decays over time, but while it lasts, it is a reservoir of power. He converts damage dealt into healing—a percentage of damage to heroes (20%) and minions (10%) returns as health, drawing on stored energy. Each time his skills hit a non-minion enemy, he gains a Combo Point (stacking to 4). Gaining a Combo Point resets the decaying timer. The crystal is not a burden—it is a gift, the last thing Fray gave him. 'I have been waiting for this,' Fredrinn says. 'Let the battle begin.' The scarring on his chest is jagged, never concealed. 'Your fear will be my guidance. Tremble in my presence.'

chapters.title: Piercing Strike, Brave Assault, Energy Eruption, and Appraiser's Wrath — The Rhythm of the Rogue
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn's skills: Piercing Strike (thrust and slow), Brave Assault (dash and knock-up), Energy Eruption (taunt, defence boost, cooldown reduction), and Appraiser's Wrath (massive crystal-energy slash that deals 175% damage at centre).
chapters.fullDesc: Fredrinn's fighting style is a rhythm of thrusts, dashes, and eruptions. Piercing Strike thrusts his sword in a line, dealing damage, slowing by 30% for 2 seconds, and enhancing his next basic attack. 'Shall I demonstrate the appraisal for you?' Brave Assault dashes in a direction, damaging the first non-minion enemy hit; his next basic attack knocks the target airborne for 0.3 seconds. 'Brave like a lion.' Energy Eruption deals damage to nearby enemies, taunts them for 1 second, grants 25-40 physical and magic defence for 3 seconds, and reduces cooldowns of Piercing Strike and Brave Assault by 75%. Consumes 1 Combo Point. 'Now, I see through everything.' Appraiser's Wrath, his ultimate, slams his sword in a fan-shaped area after a brief delay, dealing massive physical damage plus a portion of stored Crystal Energy. Enemies at the centre take 175% increased damage. Consumes 3 Combo Points. 'Appraisal is completed.'

chapters.title: The Network of the Money-Grubber
chapters.shortDesc: In Los Pecados, Fredrinn cultivated a reputation as a gold-obsessed 'money-grubber' to hide his true purpose. He built a network of smugglers, thieves, and informants to feed him clues about Fray.
chapters.fullDesc: Los Pecados was a city of sin, lawless frontier where the only law was gold—perfect for a man who needed information. Fredrinn became known as a 'money-grubber,' a treasure hunter obsessed with wealth. It was a reputation he cultivated deliberately. The less people knew about his true purpose, the safer he was. He built a network of contacts: smugglers who knew the desert routes, thieves who had stolen maps from imperial archives, information brokers with ears in every tavern. He paid them generously. Sometimes the scraps led to dead ends, ruins picked clean centuries ago, traps and monsters. But sometimes they led to something real—a map matching Fray's descriptions, an inscription mentioning a ritual of disappearance, a rumour of a ghost haunting the ruins where Fray vanished. Fredrinn followed every lead. He never gave up.

chapters.title: The Crystal's Secret
chapters.shortDesc: Research revealed the crystal might be linked to a lost civilisation that stored energy in crystalline form. Fredrinn learned to listen to its hum, feeling it pulse at ancient ruins—a possible beacon to find Fray.
chapters.fullDesc: The crystal was more than a power source—it was a key. Research revealed that the gem might be linked to a lost civilisation, a people who had mastered storing energy in crystalline form, who had built the altar that swallowed Fray. The crystal was a fragment of a larger network, a puzzle spanning centuries. Fredrinn studied it with the same intensity Fray had brought to their explorations. He learned to listen to its hum, to feel its pulse, to sense the energy flowing through it. The crystal responded to certain locations—ancient ruins, hidden temples where ley lines converged. It would pulse brighter, hum louder, almost as if trying to communicate. Fredrinn wondered if Fray could feel it too, if the crystal was a beacon that could guide him back. He clung to that hope. It was all he had.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Rogue Appraiser
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn does not know if Fray is alive or dead. But he will keep searching, fighting, never giving up. He is the Rogue Appraiser, and he will never stop looking for his lost friend.
chapters.fullDesc: Fredrinn does not know what the future holds. He does not know if Fray is alive or dead, if the crystal can ever be removed, if he will ever find the answers he seeks. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will search. He will fight. He will never give up. The crystal pulses. The compass spins. The rogue appraiser waits. He is Fredrinn, the Rogue Appraiser. And he will never stop looking for his lost friend. 'Aku mungkin tidak bisa memperbaiki kesalahan masa lalu, tapi satu hal yang bisa kulakukan adalah mencari kebenaran bersama orang yang kupercaya.' 'I may not be able to fix past mistakes, but the one thing I can do is seek the truth with the people I trust.'

chapters.title: The Compass That Finally Points
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn stands on a dune overlooking Los Pecados, compass spinning, crystal pulsing. He feels Fray's presence and whispers, 'I will find you. I promised.' The search continues.
chapters.fullDesc: "They call me the Rogue Appraiser. I did not choose the name. I do not care about names. I care about the compass—the broken, spinning, maddening compass that Fray left behind. I am Fredrinn. I am the son who walked away. I am the friend who stayed. I am the treasure hunter who has been searching for a ghost for longer than I care to remember. And I will never stop." — Fredrinn, standing on a dune overlooking Los Pecados, the compass in his hand, the crystal pulsing in his chest. The night is warm, the stars bright. The needle is spinning—it always spins. But sometimes, when he closes his eyes and listens to the crystal's hum, he feels a presence. A warmth. A whisper. Fray is out there somewhere. Waiting. Watching. Fredrinn smiles—a sad smile, but not without hope. 'I will find you. I promised.' He walks back toward the city, the compass spinning in his hand. The search continues.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Fredrinn's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Crystalline Armour (damage storage and healing, Combo Points), Piercing Strike (slow, enhanced basic attack), Brave Assault (dash, knock-up), Energy Eruption (taunt, defence boost, cooldown reduction), and Appraiser's Wrath (centre-damage ultimate).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: rooted in the crystal Fray entrusted to him—merged with his heart, storing damage as energy and converting it into healing. He fights with a broadsword etched with runes.

Crystalline Armour (Passive): stores damage as Crystal Energy (decays 10% max HP per second after 5s). Converts 20% of damage to heroes (10% to minions) into healing. Gains 1 Combo Point (max 4) when skills hit non-minion enemies; gaining a point resets the decay timer.

Piercing Strike (Skill 1): thrusts in a direction, dealing 125-250 (+7% Total HP) (+120% Extra Physical Attack) physical damage, slowing by 30% for 2s, and enhancing next basic attack (extra range, 85-135 (+100% Total Physical Attack) damage). 200% damage to non-heroes. Cooldown 7.5-6.5s.

Brave Assault (Skill 2): dashes, dealing 140-215 (+80% Extra Physical Attack) damage to first non-minion enemy hit; enhanced basic attack knocks airborne for 0.3s. Cooldown 7.5-6.5s.

Energy Eruption (Skill 3): deals 210-300 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) damage to nearby enemies, taunts for 1s, grants 25-40 Physical/Magic Defence for 3s, and reduces cooldowns of Skill 1 and Skill 2 by 75%. Consumes 1 Combo Point. Cooldown 8s.

Appraiser's Wrath (Ultimate): after a brief delay, slams sword in a fan-shaped area, dealing 600-1000 (+100% Extra Physical Attack) (+40% Stored Crystal Energy) physical damage. Enemies at the centre take 175% increased damage. Consumes 3 Combo Points. Cooldown 24-20s.

The Aura of the Rogue Appraiser: a faint hum, a crackle of crystal energy—allies feel protected, enemies feel the crystal's hunger.

chapters.title: On the Rogue Appraiser
chapters.shortDesc: Fredrinn will be the Rogue Appraiser not because he wants to be, but because someone has to carry the crystal and search for the lost. He will never stop searching.
chapters.fullDesc: Rogue Appraiser. The title is a burden and a gift. It reminds Fredrinn of the father who cast him out, the brother who saved him, the friend he has been searching for all these years. He does not know if he will ever be worthy. But he knows he will try. Every day, in every battle, with every swing. He will be resilient, relentless, hopeful. He will be the Rogue Appraiser. Not because he wants to be. Because he has to be. Because someone has to carry the crystal and search for the lost. And Fredrinn, the son who walked away, the friend who stayed, the treasure hunter of Los Pecados, has decided that someone will be him. The night is dark. The crystal pulses. The compass spins. And Fredrinn never stops searching.

chapters.title: The Rose That Learned to Bleed
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot introduces himself as the Perfumed Knight, the prodigal son of House Baroque who fell from grace through arrogance, found humility in defeat, and discovered true love with Odette, the Swan Princess.
chapters.fullDesc: "They say I was born with a silver sword in my hand and a crown of roses on my head. They say I was the perfect noble—handsome, talented, adored by all who laid eyes upon me. They are not wrong. I was the pride of House Baroque, the greatest fencer of my generation, the man who could make a blade sing. I had wealth, status, beauty, and the admiration of the masses. I thought I was invincible. I thought the world existed for my pleasure. I was wrong. Arrogance is a poison that seeps into the soul and rots it from within. I drank deeply of that poison. I caroused, I brawled, I broke hearts without a second thought. I was the prodigal son, the disappointment, the man my father erased from the family records. Then I met a woman who saw through my masks, who touched my wounds with gentle hands, who showed me that there was more to life than pleasure and pride. I am Lancelot, the Perfumed Knight. I am the brother of Guinevere, the best friend of a street fighter who cannot dress himself, and the protector of a princess who taught me what it means to love. I have made mistakes. I have hurt those who loved me. But I am trying to be better. That is the only redemption there is."

chapters.title: The Gilded Cradle of Castle Gorge
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot was born into House Baroque, one of the most powerful noble families, known for their fencing art. He was a prodigy—beautiful, talented, adored—and he began to believe his own legend.
chapters.fullDesc: Castle Gorge was a palace of marble halls, rose gardens, golden fountains. The Baroque family ruled for centuries, their wealth from gold mines. Their greatest art was fencing—elegant, precise, deadly. Lancelot was the eldest son. He picked up a rapier at four, defeated opponents twice his age by six, mastered advanced techniques by ten. The masters said, 'He has the true gift. We have nothing left to teach him.' Lancelot basked in the praise. He was beautiful, talented, wealthy. He had everything. He began to believe his own legend. The arrogance came naturally, like breathing. He thought he was better than everyone else, that rules did not apply to him.

chapters.title: The Smothering Love of the Duke
chapters.shortDesc: Duke Baroque, Lancelot's father, expressed love through expectations and pressure. He arranged a political marriage for Lancelot. Lancelot refused, stormed out of Castle Gorge, and was erased from the family records.
chapters.fullDesc: Duke Baroque loved his son through demands—'You must be perfect, strong, wise. The family's future rests on your shoulders.' Lancelot wanted to be free—to fence, drink, enjoy pleasure. When he was eighteen, the Duke arranged a political marriage to a noblewoman Lancelot had never met. 'It is for the good of the family.' 'I do not care about the good of the family.' The argument lasted hours, words exchanged that could not be taken back. Lancelot stormed out, vowing never to return. He did not say goodbye to his sister Guinevere, who watched from a window with tears in her eyes. He was done with duty, family, House Baroque. He was free.

chapters.title: The Prodigal's Wanderings
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot travelled across the empire, drinking, duelling, seducing. He burned through his inheritance and made enemies everywhere. The fun soured; he became emotionally empty and alone.
chapters.fullDesc: Freedom was not what Lancelot imagined. He travelled across the Moniyan Empire, drinking in taverns, duelling in streets, seducing women in castles. He spent money like water, burned through his inheritance, made enemies wherever he went. The nobles whispered about the prodigal son, the fallen prince. Lancelot did not care—until the fun soured. Drinking lost its appeal. Duels became routine. Women blurred together, faces indistinguishable, names forgotten. He was alone—not physically, but emotionally, spiritually. He began to wonder if his father had been right: maybe he was a disappointment, worthless, nothing more than a handsome face and a quick blade. Doubt gnawed at him. Emptiness grew. He sought refuge in the bottle.

chapters.title: The Drunken Brawl and the Lake of Blood
chapters.shortDesc: In a tavern near Azure Lake, Lancelot drunkenly attacked passing elves. He was ambushed, wounded, and fled into the freezing waters of Azure Lake, where he nearly died.
chapters.fullDesc: The Rusty Anchor was a dive where wine was cheap and fights frequent. Lancelot had been drinking for hours when a group of elves passed through. In drunken arrogance, he challenged them. They refused. He insulted them. They walked away. He pursued. The first few fights were easy; the elves fell before his blade. He pursued survivors into the mountains, where they regrouped in the high passes. Lancelot stumbled into their trap. They attacked from all sides with blinding, freezing magic. He was wounded—a dozen cuts, a cracked rib, a gash across his chest. He fled, plunging into the cold waters of Azure Lake, swimming until his arms gave out. He floated, helpless, waiting for death.

chapters.title: The Hands That Healed
chapters.shortDesc: Odette, the Swan Princess, found Lancelot floating in the lake. She carried him to Swan Castle and tended his wounds for weeks, refusing to accept the healers' verdict that he would not survive.
chapters.fullDesc: Odette, princess of Swan Castle, found Lancelot at dawn. She saw a body floating in the water—a handsome man, golden hair tangled with weeds, blue lips barely moving. She waded in, pulled him to shore, carried him to the castle. The healers said he would not survive—wounds too deep, blood loss too severe, infection spreading. Odette refused. She tended him herself: cleaned wounds, changed bandages, fed broth. She stayed by his bedside for days, for weeks. Lancelot drifted in and out of consciousness, dreaming of fire and blood and a soft, kind voice. When he finally opened his eyes, he saw a woman with hair like spun gold and eyes like the summer sky. 'Where am I?' 'Swan Castle. You are safe.'

chapters.title: The Awakening of the Heart
chapters.shortDesc: During his recovery, Lancelot fell in love with Odette. Her kindness, without judgement, made him want to be a better man. He took her hand, and something between them shifted forever.
chapters.fullDesc: The weeks that followed were the quietest of Lancelot's life. Odette visited every day with books, flowers, stories. She did not ask about his past or judge his mistakes. She simply was—a presence, a warmth, a light. Lancelot looked forward to her visits. He thought about her when she was not there. He wanted to be a better man, not for himself, but for her. 'You are not what I expected,' she said. 'What did you expect?' 'Someone arrogant, cruel, who would not care that I saved his life.' 'And what do you see now?' 'A man who is lost. A man trying to find his way home.' He reached out and took her hand. She did not pull away. Something shifted between them that day—something that would change both their lives forever.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Perfumed Knight
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Lancelot: over six feet tall, lean, golden-blonde hair, piercing blue eyes, chocolate-brown tunic with open chest, sapphire-blue capelet, silver armoured boots, and the rapier Rose Thorn.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Lancelot is to see a man sculpted by beauty and broken by pride. He stands over six feet, lean and graceful. His face has a sharp aristocratic jawline, high cheekbones, a straight nose. His eyes are piercing crystalline blue. His hair is a voluminous golden-blonde mane, falling in wavy layers to his shoulders. His upper body wears a deep chocolate-brown tunic open at the chest, revealing a toned torso and a ruffled white cravat with a glowing cyan gemstone. A gold-plated pauldron with a stylised blue rose adorns his right shoulder, from which a sapphire-blue capelet drapes down his back. His hands are in dark leather bracers. He wears form-fitting dark charcoal trousers tucked into elaborate knee-high silver boots with gold floral engravings. His weapon is the rapier Rose Thorn—a long, slender blade with a circular golden bell guard. His aura is a fragrance of roses—a mix of floral grace and deadly intent.

chapters.title: Puncture — The Charge That Never Ends
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot's signature mobility technique: a charging thrust that deals damage, applies a Sword Mark, and resets its cooldown if the target is not already marked, allowing chain charges.
chapters.fullDesc: Puncture is Lancelot's signature technique—a charging thrust that closes distance quickly, deals physical damage, and applies a Sword Mark to the target. He launches forward, blade extended, body low. If the target does not already bear the Sword Mark, Puncture's cooldown resets, allowing him to charge again—and again, dancing through the battlefield, striking multiple enemies. The technique is the essence of fencing: a lunge, pure and simple, executed with perfect form and devastating speed. Puncture is exhausting; each charge drains stamina, and close range leaves him vulnerable. He uses it to mark high-value targets, to close distance, to set up his ultimate. But when he uses it, he uses it with all the grace in his trained body.

chapters.title: Thorned Rose and Phantom Execution — The Dance of Invincibility
chapters.shortDesc: Thorned Rose is a series of rapid thrusts that make Lancelot untargetable. Phantom Execution is his ultimate: an untargetable charge ending in a massive slash, immune to damage.
chapters.fullDesc: Thorned Rose is Lancelot's area-control technique—a series of rapid thrusts in a fan-shaped area, striking enemies up to three times. During the technique, he is untargetable, his body flickering like a phantom as his blade sings. Each strike slows enemies; stacks accumulate until they can barely move. Thorned Rose is not exhausting; he can use it often, though each use leaves him momentarily vulnerable. Phantom Execution is his ultimate—a breathtaking, untargetable charge that ends in a single, massive slash. He charges forward, body flickering, immune to damage, blade trailing phantom light. The damage is devastating, capable of finishing wounded enemies. Phantom Execution is exhausting—each use drains his reserves completely. He can use it only once per battle, but when he uses it, he uses it with all the fury in his reformed heart.

chapters.title: The Return to Castle Gorge
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot returned to Castle Gorge a changed, humbler man. His father had erased him from family records. Lancelot apologised; his father walked away in silence.
chapters.fullDesc: Lancelot returned to Castle Gorge humbler, quieter, more thoughtful. His father had struck his name from family records, disowned him, pretended he never existed. The servants whispered he was not welcome. Lancelot did not argue. 'Father, I have come to apologise.' The Duke looked at him with cold eyes. 'Apologies are cheap. What have you done to earn my forgiveness?' 'I have done nothing. I have only begun to understand how much I have wronged you.' The Duke was silent for a long moment, then turned and walked away. Lancelot did not follow. He had said what he needed to say. The rest was up to his father.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Never Stopped Loving
chapters.shortDesc: Guinevere, Lancelot's sister, welcomed him back with open arms. She had become a powerful anti-gravity sorceress. They reconciled, and he told her about his love for Odette.
chapters.fullDesc: Guinevere was waiting in the rose garden. No longer the little girl who watched him leave with tears, she was now a woman—beautiful, talented, fierce. She had trained at the Magic Academy, mastered anti-gravity sorcery, become a hero. 'Brother.' 'Sister.' She ran to him and threw her arms around his neck. He held her, feeling the warmth of her embrace, the forgiveness in her touch. 'I am sorry.' 'I know. I have always known.' They sat in the garden for hours, talking, laughing, remembering. She told him about her studies and her plans. He told her about his wanderings, his wounds, his love for Odette. 'You have changed,' she said. 'I hope so,' he replied.

chapters.title: The Legacy of the Perfumed Knight
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot does not know if his father will forgive him or if he will be worthy of Odette's love. But he will fight, protect, and love. He will never stop trying.
chapters.fullDesc: Lancelot does not know what the future holds. He does not know if his father will ever forgive him, if he will ever be worthy of Odette's love, if the scars of his past will ever fully heal. But he knows what he will do in the meantime. He will fight. He will protect. He will love. The blade never stops. The rose never fades. The knight never yields. He is Lancelot, the Perfumed Knight. And he will never stop trying to be worthy of the second chance he has been given.

chapters.title: The Rose That Finally Bloomed
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot stands on the balcony of Swan Castle, watching over Odette as she sleeps. He does not know if he is worthy, but he will protect her forever.
chapters.fullDesc: "They call me the Perfumed Knight. I did not choose the name. I did not want it. But I have carried it for many years now, and I have learned that names are just words. What matters is what you do. And what I do is protect those I love. That is enough." — Lancelot, to Odette, as they watched the swans glide across the lake. The night is quiet over Swan Castle. Lancelot stands on the balcony overlooking Azure Lake, rapier resting beside him. Odette is inside, sleeping. He watches over her, as he has since she saved his life. He thinks about his father who has not forgiven him, his sister who never stopped loving him, the woman who showed him what love means. He does not know if he is worthy. But he knows what he will do: fight, protect, love. The blade waits. The rose blooms. The knight stands ready. And as long as Lancelot draws breath, someone will protect those who cannot protect themselves.

chapters.title: A Compendium of Lancelot's Powers
chapters.shortDesc: Detailed breakdown of Soul Cutter (passive damage increase), Puncture (charging thrust with reset), Thorned Rose (untargetable fan thrusts), and Phantom Execution (untargetable ultimate slash).
chapters.fullDesc:
The Nature of His Power: rooted in fencing mastery—no magic, no blessings, only blade, skill, and will. Speed is his weapon.

Soul Cutter (Passive): each charge increases damage by 7.5% for 4 seconds, stacking up to 4 times (30% total).

Puncture (Skill 1): charges forward, dealing physical damage and applying a Sword Mark. If the target has no Sword Mark, cooldown resets, allowing chain charges. Damage: physical (+% Total Physical Attack).

Thorned Rose (Skill 2): rapid thrusts in a fan-shaped area, striking enemies up to 3 times. Untargetable during the technique. Each strike slows enemies. Cooldown short.

Phantom Execution (Ultimate): charges forward in an untargetable state, ending with a single massive slash dealing devastating physical damage. Can be used once per battle; drains reserves.

The Aura of the Perfumed Knight: a fragrance of roses—inspiring allies, unsettling enemies.

chapters.title: On the Perfumed Knight
chapters.shortDesc: Lancelot will be the Perfumed Knight not because he wants to be, but because someone has to protect those who cannot protect themselves—and he has decided that someone will be him.
chapters.fullDesc: Perfumed Knight. The title is a burden and a gift. It reminds Lancelot of his father who disowned him, his sister who never stopped loving him, Odette who saved his life. He does not know if he will ever be worthy. But he knows he will try. Every day, in every battle, with every thrust. He will be graceful, deadly, kind. He will be the Perfumed Knight. Not because he wants to be. Because he has to be. Because someone has to protect those who cannot protect themselves. And Lancelot, the prodigal son of House Baroque, the brother of Guinevere, the lover of Odette, has decided that someone will be him. The night is dark. The blade is ready. The rose blooms eternal. And Lancelot never stops dancing.

chapters.title: The Song That Would Not Die
chapters.shortDesc: Odette introduces herself as the Swan Princess, the thirteenth-generation heiress of Swan Castle. She left her sheltered life for love, defying her family's legacy of peaceful obscurity to find her own voice.
chapters.fullDesc: "Forgive me, Grandfather, for the life I have chosen. Not the life you built—the quiet life, the peaceful life, the life of politics avoided and thrones relinquished. I know you abdicated the crown so that House Alvin could exist in the shadows, so that we could be forgotten, so that we could be safe. But safety is not happiness, and peace is not purpose. I have met a man who sees me—not the princess, not the heiress, not the thirteenth-generation keeper of a legacy I never asked for. He sees me. And in his eyes, I have found a courage I did not know I possessed. I am leaving the castle. I am leaving the lake. I am leaving the life you built for me. And I am not afraid." — Odette, in a letter left on the windowsill of her tower on the night she departed Swan Castle. She was born in the highest tower, on a night when the moon was full and the swans were singing. She grew up surrounded by magic and music, the pearl of Azure Lake. But she was restless, yearning for adventure. Then she found a wounded knight on the shore—Lancelot—and fell in love. Now she has left everything behind, following her heart into the unknown. This is her story.

chapters.title: The Castle by the Lake
chapters.shortDesc: Swan Castle, built by Alvin I who abdicated the throne for love, has been home to House Alvin for thirteen generations. Odette grew up surrounded by nature, magic, and the gentle Lakeshore Ambience.
chapters.fullDesc: Azure Lake sits in the southern hills of the Moniyan Empire, a sapphire tucked into the mountains. On its northern shore stands Swan Castle—not a fortress, but a palace of white stone, tall windows, and gardens of roses and lilies. For thirteen generations, House Alvin has called it home. The first Prince Alvin gave up the throne to marry a woman of humble birth, choosing love over power. His descendants carried on his legacy, valuing happiness over status. Odette, the thirteenth-generation heiress, grew up in this world. She sang to the swans, played with the animals, and learned the magic of Lakeshore Ambience from her father. 'Go outside and look around,' he would say. 'Every tree and flower will make you feel the vitality everywhere. Sing, my child, and then you will feel the love of nature.' Odette sang. And nature answered.

chapters.title: The Legacy of Alvin I
chapters.shortDesc: The story of Prince Alvin I, who abdicated the throne for love, was Odette's favourite. She understood her family's choice but felt the walls of Swan Castle closing in—she wanted more than peaceful obscurity.
chapters.fullDesc: The story of the first Prince Alvin was Odette's favourite bedtime story. He was handsome, brave, destined to be emperor. But he fell in love with a commoner. The emperor forbade the match. Alvin I abdicated, gave up the throne, and built Swan Castle by the most beautiful lake in the empire. Odette loved the story because it showed her family's character: heroes who chose love over power. But the story also contained a warning. By abdicating, Alvin I had forfeited his family's claim to the throne. The Alvins rarely got involved in domestic politics. Odette understood this, but she did not agree with it. 'You have the right to the throne,' she once told her grandfather. 'Rights are not the same as responsibilities,' he replied. Odette filed the conversation away. She was not content to simply live in peace. She wanted adventure, excitement, love. She wanted to live.

chapters.title: The Caged Bird and the Open Sky
chapters.shortDesc: As Odette grew older, Swan Castle began to feel like a cage. She threw herself into her magic, mastering the Lakeshore Ambience, but the loneliness never left. She longed for a true companion.
chapters.fullDesc: The walls of Swan Castle began to feel less like protection and more like a cage. Her family loved her, but their vision of 'what was best' was rooted in the past—stay out of affairs, keep heads down, be content. Odette was not content. She spent more time at the lake, confiding in the swans. 'I want to leave,' she whispered. 'I want to see the world. I want to fall in love.' The swans could not answer, but they stayed with her. She threw herself into training, mastering the Lakeshore Ambience, perfecting spells passed down through generations. But the loneliness never fully went away. She was adored by thousands, called the pearl left over by the gods of the mortal realm. Yet Odette felt unbearably lonely. She had never had a true companion. She had never been in love. But she felt something coming—something that would change everything. And she was ready.

chapters.title: The Anatomy of a Swan Princess
chapters.shortDesc: A detailed description of Odette: 165 cm, slender and graceful, honey-blonde hair, warm brown eyes, white and silver bodice with a blue gem, translucent feather cape, magical staff, and dueling sword.
chapters.fullDesc: To look at Odette is to see a woman shaped by centuries of romantic legacy and gentle magic. She stands 165 centimetres, slender and graceful, with the physique of a dancer. Her face has delicate features, a soft jawline, high cheekbones, and fair, smooth skin. Her eyes are deep warm brown—the colour of earth after rain—but when she sings, they seem to glow. Her hair is rich honey-blonde, often styled in elegant curls, with a silver tiara on her brow. She wears a white and silver bodice with a sweetheart neckline, silver filigree, and a glowing blue gem at her chest—a focus for her magic.
